new.text:
On R43-M0, two KERNEL FATAL "kernel panic" log lines (pattern 576) were logged within the same second, on R43-M0-NC-I:J18-U01 and R43-M0-N8-I:J18-U11. The logs show no other lines before or after them in the context windows checked, so nothing in the logs explains the cause.
Scope: bgl dataset only. Main window 2005-08-19 13:26:00 → 14:26:00 (all locations), plus ±1 h on location R43/R43-M0. Pattern 576 history covers 2005-06-03 → 2006-01-04, and the R43 background sample covers 2005-08-18 12:00 → 2005-08-20 12:00. The location filters 'R43/M0' and 'R43-M0' returned 0 matches (wrong format); 'R43/R43-M0' works. The R43 two-day sample was truncated (30 of 125 lines shown), so counts from it are not exhaustive.
First line: 2005-08-19 13:56:00.280831, KERNEL FATAL, node R43-M0-NC-I:J18-U01, body "kernel panic" (line_id 3069219, pattern_id 576).
Last line: 2005-08-19 13:56:00.628434, KERNEL FATAL, node R43-M0-N8-I:J18-U11, body "kernel panic" (line_id 3069220, pattern_id 576). The window 2005-08-19 13:50:00 → 14:05:00 holds 2 log lines on 2 nodes, and both are this pattern.
Timeline before: 0 log lines precede the first panic within 3600 s on R43/R43-M0, and 0 log lines precede it within 1800 s across all locations.
Timeline after: only 1 log line follows the first panic within the window, the second "kernel panic" on R43-M0-N8-I:J18-U11. Nothing else was logged within 1800 s, in any location.
Earlier context: on 2005-08-18 around 12:40, INFO lines (pattern_id 584) from the same R43-M0 nodes read "ciod: generated 64 core files for program /bgl/apps/swl-prep/ibm-swl/functional/sppm_chkpt/run/sppm". Examples: R43-M0-N8-I:J18-U11 at 2005-08-18 12:40:17.079286 and R43-M0-NC-I:J18-U01 at 2005-08-18 12:40:29.182967.
New vs recurring: pattern 576 ("kernel panic", team node-platform) has 18 log lines, 13 bursts and 18 nodes over 8 weeks active, first seen 2005-08-15T16:31:53.274944. As of this event it had 2 bursts and 3 log lines before it, so it was not new.
Rate vs usual: the week of 2005-08-15 has 3 bursts and 5 log lines for this pattern. The median gap between bursts is 5 days, 1:01:37.812071 and the longest is 20 days, 21:52:18.514888.
Local vs spread: from 2005-08-15 to 2005-08-26, pattern 576 has 10 log lines on 10 distinct nodes. Earlier lines were on R04-M0-N8-I:J18-U01 (2005-08-15 16:31:53.274944), R24-M1-N4-I:J18-U11 and R10-M0-N4-I:J18-U11. Later lines were on R57, R66 and R67 on 2005-08-23.
Hypothesis: The panics may be one occurrence of a recurring, job- or software-related fault that also panicked nodes in other racks (R04, R24, R10 and later R57, R66, R67), rather than a hardware fault specific to R43-M0. Would confirm: Check which job ran on R43-M0 at 2005-08-19 13:56 and whether the other pattern 576 bursts ran the same program. Run precursors for pattern_id 576 and compare with the ciod core-file lines (pattern 584).
Unknown: Root cause: the log body is only "kernel panic" with no stack, error code or job id.
Unknown: Why nothing was logged around the panics, e.g. whether the nodes stopped logging or logging is sparse.
Unknown: Which job or workload was running, and any impact on users or downtime; none of this is in the logs.
Unknown: Whether the 2005-08-18 core-file lines are related to the 2005-08-19 panics; they are about a day apart and the sample was truncated.
Next step: Run search_logs with pattern_id 584 and location R43/R43-M0 for 2005-08-18 12:43 → 2005-08-19 13:56, then run precursors(576) and spread(576). — The windows before the panic were empty, so the only nearby evidence is the 2005-08-18 core-file lines and the other pattern 576 bursts.
Next step: Inspect the kernel and console output of R43-M0-NC-I:J18-U01 and R43-M0-N8-I:J18-U11 outside the log table, and check the job scheduler record for the 13:56 run. — The logged body is just "kernel panic", so the cause has to come from the node console or job data.

old.text:
Two I/O-node (J18) kernel panics (KERNEL, FATAL, pattern 576) hit R43-M0 within a second of each other at 2005-08-19 13:56:00. Nothing else was logged in the dataset in the minutes around them. The previous R43-M0 lines were ciod login/link errors at 12:26 and the next were ciod login errors at 17:12.
Scope: bgl dataset only. Windows: 2005-08-19 13:50:00 → 14:02:00 (all locations), 13:00:00 → 15:00:00 (location R43), and ±24h around line 3069219 (location R43/R43-M0, truncated). Pattern 576 history covers the whole corpus (sample of 10 of 18 lines, truncated). Location filters 'R43/M0' and 'R43-M0' returned 0 lines, so the R43 and full-path filters were used instead.
Line 3069219 at 2005-08-19 13:56:00.280831: KERNEL FATAL 'kernel panic' on node R43-M0-NC-I:J18-U01 (pattern_id 576).
Line 3069220 at 2005-08-19 13:56:00.628434: KERNEL FATAL 'kernel panic' on node R43-M0-N8-I:J18-U11 (pattern_id 576). This is the last panic on R43 in the window.
Across 2005-08-19 13:00 → 15:00, R43 had 2 matching log lines on 2 distinct nodes, first 2005-08-19 13:56:00.280831 and last 2005-08-19 13:56:00.628434.
In the whole bgl dataset between 13:50:00 and 14:02:00 there were 2 log lines in total, both on R43-M0 (R43-M0-N8-I:J18-U11 and R43-M0-NC-I:J18-U01, 1 line each), so no other location logged anything in that window.
In the ±900s context around the first panic (all scope) there were 0 log lines before it and 1 after it (the second panic).
Before: the closest earlier R43/R43-M0 lines were at 2005-08-19 12:26:09 to 12:26:12, e.g. 'ciod: Error reading message prefix after LOGIN_MESSAGE on CioStream socket to 172.16.96.116:40778: Link has been severed' on R43-M0-N8-I:J18-U01 and 'ciod: LOGIN chdir(/home/auselton/testing) failed: No such file or directory' on R43-M0-NC-I:J18-U01 (line 3069103, 12:26:12.894104). Similar chdir failures on N0 and N4 nodes were logged at 12:24:59 to 12:25:05.
After: the next R43/R43-M0 lines were at 2005-08-19 17:12:37.933881 onward, e.g. 'ciod: LOGIN chdir(/home/auselton/testing) failed: No such file or directory' on R43-M0-N8-I:J18-U11, plus a 'Link has been severed' line at 17:12:38.028933 on R43-M0-N8-I:J18-U01. The same chdir message also appeared on N4, N0 and NC nodes through 17:12:45.869660.

new.text:
The ciod daemon on BGL I/O nodes lost its CioStream socket to 172.16.96.116, logging FATAL "Error reading message prefix ... Link has been severed". It first appeared at 2005-11-17 05:33:24.623263 on R77-M0-NC-I:J18-U11, directly after that node logged "ciod: Received signal 15". The pattern was new, with no matching log lines in the prior 168 hours.
Scope: Dataset bgl. Main window 2005-11-17 00:00:00 → 2005-11-18 00:00:00, with context from 2005-11-17 05:18:24 to 05:33:54 and a baseline of 2005-11-10 05:30:00 → 2005-11-17 05:30:00. Filters: text "Error reading message prefix" / "Link has been severed", pattern 968. The search and context results are truncated samples, so counts come from the totals. The all-time facet counts cover five patterns that match the text query.
First matching line: line_id 4215995 at 2005-11-17 05:33:24.623263, component APP, severity FATAL, node R77-M0-NC-I:J18-U11: "ciod: Error reading message prefix on CioStream socket to 172.16.96.116:43572, Link has been severed".
On 2005-11-17 the query matched 1008 log lines on 504 distinct nodes, from 2005-11-17 05:33:24.623263 to 2005-11-17 06:17:09.268580.
Burst 1 of pattern 968 ran from 2005-11-17 05:33:24.623263 to 2005-11-17 05:37:00.983282 and covered 504 log lines on 504 nodes. The pattern is owned by team hpc-workloads.
The line immediately before the first error is on the same node, line_id 4215994 at 2005-11-17 05:33:24.491562, KERNEL INFO: "ciod: Received signal 15, code=0, errno=0, address=0x000001b0".
The same pairing recurs on the next nodes. On R77-M0-N4-I:J18-U11, "ciod: Received signal 15, code=0, errno=0, address=0x000001b0" (05:33:24.852317) is followed by the FATAL "Error reading message prefix ..." line (05:33:24.982940). R77-M1-NC-I:J18-U01 and R77-M1-N8-I:J18-U11 show the same sequence.
Before that, the context window shows INFO torus lines on R63 nodes, for example "4167003 torus sender x- retransmission error(s) (dcr 0x02f5) detected and corrected over 76 seconds" and "1 torus receiver x- input pipe error(s) (dcr 0x02ed) detected and corrected over 43 seconds". These are on different nodes from the first error.
Earlier in the same sequence, pattern 959 first appeared at 2005-11-17 05:12:38.788692 on 64 nodes with 64 log lines, severity FATAL: "ciod: Error loading /bgl/apps/followup/HPL/xhpl.<N>: invalid or missing program image, Permission denied".
Pattern 960 ("ciod: Received signal <N>, code=<N>, errno=<N>, address=<HEX>") first appeared at 2005-11-17 05:14:17.105933, with 424 log lines on 376 nodes in the sequence window.
Spread: the sampled error lines come from racks R77, R40, R41, R54 and R56. Across the whole dataset the matching lines cover 1024 distinct nodes.
The pattern was new. There were 0 bursts and 0 log lines of pattern 968 before 2005-11-17 05:33:00. The baseline over 168 earlier hourly windows had 0 lines (baseline rate 0.0 per hour) against 1008 lines in the 1-hour window starting 2005-11-17 05:30:00.
The pattern then recurred. Pattern 968 has 82 bursts and 26546 log lines over the dataset, active in 8 weeks, with the last line at 2006-01-03T11:56:38.877831. The week of 2005-11-14 had 3 bursts and 1211 log lines, and the week of 2005-11-21 had 22 bursts and 8685 log lines.
Hypothesis: ciod on the I/O nodes was terminated by signal 15 (the same line precedes the error on each sampled node), for example when jobs were killed or the control system tore down the partition. That closed the CioStream sockets to 172.16.96.116 and produced "Link has been severed" on each node. The earlier failed xhpl load (Permission denied) may belong to the same job lifecycle. Would confirm: Check that every one of the 504 nodes logs "Received signal 15" shortly before its error. Find who or what sent the signal, and check the job and partition events around 05:12-05:34 for the xhpl run. If signal 15 is absent on some nodes, the hypothesis is weakened.
Unknown: The logs do not show who or what sent signal 15, nor the root cause of the severed link.
Unknown: The logs do not show whether the Permission denied xhpl load error (pattern 959) caused the later socket errors; they show only that it came earlier.
Unknown: Job impact, downtime and customer impact are not in these logs.
Unknown: Only a sample of the 1008 lines and of the surrounding lines was retrieved, so per-node ordering across all 504 nodes is unverified.
Next step: Run get_context or search_logs for "Received signal 15" (pattern 960) on 2005-11-17 05:30:00 → 05:40:00, then compare the node set against the 504 nodes with pattern 968 and check the signal-before-error ordering per node. — The signal 15 line immediately precedes the first error on the nodes sampled, and 960 spans 376 nodes in the sequence window.
Next step: Inspect the job and control-system events for /bgl/apps/followup/HPL/xhpl, around the 05:12:38 permission failure and the 05:33:24 error burst, and check the logs of the peer host 172.16.96.116. — The Permission denied FATAL on 64 nodes precedes the burst, and every sampled error points at socket peer 172.16.96.116.
Next step: Review pattern 968 bursts against job schedules, since the pattern recurred in 82 bursts across 8 weeks after it first appeared. — The pattern is new as of 2005-11-17 but then recurs, which suggests a recurring trigger rather than a one-off.

Before the first one: no earlier log lines on node R04-M0-N3-C:J17-U11 in the node-scoped context window before it (before_total 0).

Whether this rate is usual: no baseline outside October 2005 was queried, so new vs recurring is not established.
The DDR/torus INFO lines on other nodes around the first event are not shown to be related to it.

sql: WITH b AS ( SELECT pattern_id, count(*) AS n, median(v) AS med, mad(v) AS mad, quantile_cont(v, 0.95) AS p95 FROM (SELECT pattern_id, duration_ms / 1000.0 AS v FROM logs WHERE dataset = 'openstack' AND pattern_id IN (SELECT DISTINCT pattern_id FROM logs WHERE dataset = 'openstack' AND duration_ms IS NOT NULL)) WHERE v IS NOT NULL GROUP BY 1 ), t AS (SELECT *, greatest(med + 6.0 * mad, med + 2.0) AS threshold FROM b ), f AS ( SELECT l.line_id, l.ts, l.pattern_id, l.object_id, l.request_id, l.duration_ms / 1000.0 AS value_s, l.body FROM logs l WHERE l.dataset = 'openstack' AND l.pattern_id IN (SELECT pattern_id FROM t) ) SELECT f.line_id, f.ts, f.pattern_id, f.object_id, f.request_id, round(f.value_s, 3) AS value_s, round(t.med, 3) AS median_s, round(f.value_s / t.med, 2) AS ratio, f.body FROM f JOIN t USING (pattern_id) WHERE f.value_s > t.threshold ORDER BY ratio DESC, f.ts LIMIT 30

WITH b AS ( SELECT pattern_id, count(*) AS n, median(v) AS med, mad(v) AS mad, quantile_cont(v, 0.95) AS p95 FROM (SELECT pattern_id, duration_ms / 1000.0 AS v FROM logs WHERE dataset = 'openstack' AND pattern_id IN (SELECT DISTINCT pattern_id FROM logs WHERE dataset = 'openstack' AND duration_ms IS NOT NULL)) WHERE v IS NOT NULL GROUP BY 1 ), t AS (SELECT *, greatest(med + 6.0 * mad, med + 2.0) AS threshold FROM b ), f AS ( SELECT l.line_id, l.ts, l.pattern_id, l.object_id, l.request_id, l.duration_ms / 1000.0 AS value_s, l.body FROM logs l WHERE l.dataset = 'openstack' AND l.pattern_id IN (SELECT pattern_id FROM t) ) SELECT t.pattern_id, p.template, t.n, round(t.med, 3) AS median_s, round(t.p95, 3) AS p95_s, round(t.mad, 3) AS mad_s, round(t.threshold, 3) AS threshold_s, count(*) FILTER (WHERE f.value_s > t.threshold) AS flagged FROM t JOIN patterns p ON p.dataset = 'openstack' AND p.pattern_id = t.pattern_id LEFT JOIN f ON f.pattern_id = t.pattern_id GROUP BY ALL ORDER BY flagged DESC, t.n DESC

WITH b AS ( SELECT pattern_id, count(*) AS n, median(v) AS med, mad(v) AS mad, quantile_cont(v, 0.95) AS p95 FROM (SELECT pattern_id, duration_ms / 1000.0 AS v FROM logs WHERE dataset = 'openstack' AND pattern_id IN (SELECT DISTINCT pattern_id FROM logs WHERE dataset = 'openstack' AND duration_ms IS NOT NULL)) WHERE v IS NOT NULL GROUP BY 1 ), t AS (SELECT *, greatest(med + 6.0 * mad, med + 2.0) AS threshold FROM b ), f AS ( SELECT l.line_id, l.ts, l.pattern_id, l.object_id, l.request_id, l.duration_ms / 1000.0 AS value_s, l.body FROM logs l WHERE l.dataset = 'openstack' AND l.pattern_id IN (SELECT pattern_id FROM t) ) SELECT count(*) AS total_matches, count(DISTINCT f.object_id) AS flagged_objects FROM f JOIN t USING (pattern_id) WHERE f.value_s > t.threshold

WITH b AS ( SELECT pattern_id, count(*) AS n, median(v) AS med, mad(v) AS mad, quantile_cont(v, 0.95) AS p95 FROM (SELECT pattern_id, duration_ms / 1000.0 AS v FROM logs WHERE dataset = 'openstack' AND pattern_id IN (SELECT DISTINCT pattern_id FROM logs WHERE dataset = 'openstack' AND duration_ms IS NOT NULL)) WHERE v IS NOT NULL GROUP BY 1 ), t AS (SELECT *, greatest(med + 6.0 * mad, med + 2.0) AS threshold FROM b ), f AS ( SELECT l.line_id, l.ts, l.pattern_id, l.object_id, l.request_id, l.duration_ms / 1000.0 AS value_s, l.body FROM logs l WHERE l.dataset = 'openstack' AND l.pattern_id IN (SELECT pattern_id FROM t) ) SELECT f.object_id, max(round(f.value_s / t.med, 2)) AS max_ratio, count(*) AS flagged_lines, min(f.ts) AS first_ts FROM f JOIN t USING (pattern_id) WHERE f.value_s > t.threshold AND f.object_id IS NOT NULL GROUP BY 1 ORDER BY 2 DESC LIMIT 50

Yes. Six VMs had abnormally slow spawn and build times, with the worst (a445709b-6ad0-40ec-8860-bec60b6ca0c2) taking 50.72 seconds to spawn against a median of 19.74 seconds (ratio 2.57). Five of the six slow starts fall on 2017-05-14, between 21:08 and 21:47.
Scope: Dataset openstack, corpus 2017-05-14 19:39:22.727 → 2017-05-17 06:25:06.749. Outlier rule: each pattern vs its own whole-dataset baseline, threshold = max(median + 6×MAD, median + 2 s). The outlier result was not truncated. The search sample and the component context windows were truncated, and only the object-scoped context for a445709b was complete.
The outlier scan returned 16 matching log lines across 6 flagged objects. Each of the 6 VMs has 2 flagged lines (spawn and build). The other 4 matches are HTTP request lines, not VM starts.
Baseline for 'Took N seconds to spawn the instance on the hypervisor' (n 2066): median 19.74 s, p95 21.008 s, threshold 22.26 s. Baseline for 'Took N seconds to build instance' (n 2066): median 20.55 s, p95 21.81 s, threshold 23.07 s.

1643649d-2f42-4303-bfcd-7798baec19f9: spawn 31.27 s (ratio 1.58), build 32.12 s (ratio 1.56), at 2017-05-14 21:47:20.593. ae651dff-c7ad-43d6-ac96-bbcd820ccca8: spawn 29.46 s (ratio 1.49), build 30.32 s (ratio 1.48), at 2017-05-14 21:09:11.081. d7d68893-c44f-4e7c-8d4b-0e7801d62776: spawn 26.69 s (ratio 1.35), build 27.61 s (ratio 1.34), at 2017-05-14 21:45:04.509.
f0ff0b46-b3cd-43e6-97eb-839fd1cdaa87 is the only flagged VM outside the 2017-05-14 window: spawn 22.56 s and build 23.34 s (both ratio 1.14) at 2017-05-16 16:49:11.697. Both values are only just over the thresholds.
Timeline for a445709b (object-scoped context, 14 lines before and 10 after, not truncated). Before: 'Claim successful' 21:42:42.360, 'Creating image' 21:42:43.044, 'VM Started (Lifecycle Event)' 21:43:27.498, 'VM Paused (Lifecycle Event)' 21:43:27.561, 'VM Resumed (Lifecycle Event)' 21:43:33.752, 'Instance spawned successfully.' 21:43:33.761. At: the 50.72 s spawn line. After: build line 51.59 s, then 'Terminating instance' 21:43:41.553.
After the slow start, a445709b's delete steps were normal: 'Took 1.02 seconds to destroy the instance on the hypervisor.' (baseline median 1.02 s) and 'Took 0.62 seconds to deallocate network for instance.'
The nova-compute context around a445709b shows host cp-1.slowvm1.tcloud-pg0.utah.cloudlab.us (resource audit lines). Those lines show 'Total usable vcpus: 16, total allocated vcpus: 1'. The same host name appears in the Compute_service record updated at 21:43:02.637, but the spawn lines themselves carry no node field.
Slow starts are rare: 6 flagged out of 2066 build lines. They are not isolated: five fall in the 2017-05-14 21:08:19.736 → 21:47:20.593 window, plus one on 2017-05-16.
Separate from VM start, four HTTP request lines at 2017-05-17 06:25 were also slow. Example: a metadata_data.json GET took 2.2444420 s against a median of 0.225 s (ratio 9.97), and a POST os-server-external-events took 2.1445580 s against a median of 0.095 s.
Hypothesis: The extra time in the worst case may be spent on the hypervisor between 'Creating image' (21:42:43.044) and 'VM Started' (21:43:27.498), for example slow image or disk preparation on the compute host. After 'VM Started', the log lines moved quickly to 'Instance spawned successfully.' Would confirm: Pull nova-compute/libvirt lines for the other five slow instances and compare the Creating image → VM Started gap with that of normal instances. Check host disk and image-cache I/O around 2017-05-14 21:08–21:48.
Unknown: Whether all six slow VMs ran on the same compute node: the spawn lines carry no node field, and only a445709b was tied to cp-1.slowvm1 through the surrounding context.
Unknown: The root cause of the slowness is not established by the logs.

Unknown: Customer impact or downtime is not in the logs.
Unknown: Whether the 4 HTTP outliers at 2017-05-17 06:25 relate to VM startup is not established.

Next step: Query nova-compute lines for the window 2017-05-14 21:08:19.736000 → 2017-05-14 21:47:20.593000 with filters on host cp-1.slowvm1.tcloud-pg0.utah.cloudlab.us, and check the host's disk, CPU and image-cache load during those minutes. — Five of the six slow starts fall in that window (first flagged line 2017-05-14 21:08:19.736000, last 2017-05-14 21:47:20.593000), which points to a local, time-bound cause rather than a steady regression.

sql: WITH b AS ( SELECT pattern_id, count(*) AS n, median(v) AS med, mad(v) AS mad, quantile_cont(v, 0.95) AS p95 FROM (SELECT pattern_id, duration_ms / 1000.0 AS v FROM logs WHERE dataset = 'openstack' AND pattern_id IN (SELECT DISTINCT pattern_id FROM logs WHERE dataset = 'openstack' AND duration_ms IS NOT NULL)) WHERE v IS NOT NULL GROUP BY 1 ), t AS (SELECT *, greatest(med + 6.0 * mad, med + 2.0) AS threshold FROM b ), f AS ( SELECT l.line_id, l.ts, l.pattern_id, l.object_id, l.request_id, l.duration_ms / 1000.0 AS value_s, l.body FROM logs l WHERE l.dataset = 'openstack' AND l.pattern_id IN (SELECT pattern_id FROM t) ) SELECT f.line_id, f.ts, f.pattern_id, f.object_id, f.request_id, round(f.value_s, 3) AS value_s, round(t.med, 3) AS median_s, round(f.value_s / t.med, 2) AS ratio, f.body FROM f JOIN t USING (pattern_id) WHERE f.value_s > t.threshold ORDER BY ratio DESC, f.ts LIMIT 30

WITH b AS ( SELECT pattern_id, count(*) AS n, median(v) AS med, mad(v) AS mad, quantile_cont(v, 0.95) AS p95 FROM (SELECT pattern_id, duration_ms / 1000.0 AS v FROM logs WHERE dataset = 'openstack' AND pattern_id IN (SELECT DISTINCT pattern_id FROM logs WHERE dataset = 'openstack' AND duration_ms IS NOT NULL)) WHERE v IS NOT NULL GROUP BY 1 ), t AS (SELECT *, greatest(med + 6.0 * mad, med + 2.0) AS threshold FROM b ), f AS ( SELECT l.line_id, l.ts, l.pattern_id, l.object_id, l.request_id, l.duration_ms / 1000.0 AS value_s, l.body FROM logs l WHERE l.dataset = 'openstack' AND l.pattern_id IN (SELECT pattern_id FROM t) ) SELECT t.pattern_id, p.template, t.n, round(t.med, 3) AS median_s, round(t.p95, 3) AS p95_s, round(t.mad, 3) AS mad_s, round(t.threshold, 3) AS threshold_s, count(*) FILTER (WHERE f.value_s > t.threshold) AS flagged FROM t JOIN patterns p ON p.dataset = 'openstack' AND p.pattern_id = t.pattern_id LEFT JOIN f ON f.pattern_id = t.pattern_id GROUP BY ALL ORDER BY flagged DESC, t.n DESC

WITH b AS ( SELECT pattern_id, count(*) AS n, median(v) AS med, mad(v) AS mad, quantile_cont(v, 0.95) AS p95 FROM (SELECT pattern_id, duration_ms / 1000.0 AS v FROM logs WHERE dataset = 'openstack' AND pattern_id IN (SELECT DISTINCT pattern_id FROM logs WHERE dataset = 'openstack' AND duration_ms IS NOT NULL)) WHERE v IS NOT NULL GROUP BY 1 ), t AS (SELECT *, greatest(med + 6.0 * mad, med + 2.0) AS threshold FROM b ), f AS ( SELECT l.line_id, l.ts, l.pattern_id, l.object_id, l.request_id, l.duration_ms / 1000.0 AS value_s, l.body FROM logs l WHERE l.dataset = 'openstack' AND l.pattern_id IN (SELECT pattern_id FROM t) ) SELECT count(*) AS total_matches, count(DISTINCT f.object_id) AS flagged_objects FROM f JOIN t USING (pattern_id) WHERE f.value_s > t.threshold

WITH b AS ( SELECT pattern_id, count(*) AS n, median(v) AS med, mad(v) AS mad, quantile_cont(v, 0.95) AS p95 FROM (SELECT pattern_id, duration_ms / 1000.0 AS v FROM logs WHERE dataset = 'openstack' AND pattern_id IN (SELECT DISTINCT pattern_id FROM logs WHERE dataset = 'openstack' AND duration_ms IS NOT NULL)) WHERE v IS NOT NULL GROUP BY 1 ), t AS (SELECT *, greatest(med + 6.0 * mad, med + 2.0) AS threshold FROM b ), f AS ( SELECT l.line_id, l.ts, l.pattern_id, l.object_id, l.request_id, l.duration_ms / 1000.0 AS value_s, l.body FROM logs l WHERE l.dataset = 'openstack' AND l.pattern_id IN (SELECT pattern_id FROM t) ) SELECT f.object_id, max(round(f.value_s / t.med, 2)) AS max_ratio, count(*) AS flagged_lines, min(f.ts) AS first_ts FROM f JOIN t USING (pattern_id) WHERE f.value_s > t.threshold AND f.object_id IS NOT NULL GROUP BY 1 ORDER BY 2 DESC LIMIT 50

For 2005-11-01 to 2005-11-29, the top recurring problems were the BGL ciod "Link has been severed" pattern (27 bursts, all new), the Apache mod_jk workerEnv error (134 bursts vs 8 the previous period), the Linux Out of Memory kills (83 bursts, all new), and BGL kernel panics. Investigate the ciod link-severed pattern first (hpc-workloads): it is new this period and spans 1024 nodes.
Scope: Datasets bgl, apache and linux; period 2005-11-01 00:00 to 2005-11-29 00:00; previous period 2005-10-04 to 2005-11-01. Filters: problem patterns only (p_problem >= 0.5), ranked by bursts. The bgl and apache top-pattern lists are truncated to 20 rows (126 and 21 matches respectively); linux is not truncated (17 matches). Bursts are recurrences with a 30-minute gap; lines are log entries.
BGL pattern 968 (ciod: Error reading message prefix on CioStream socket, Link has been severed; team hpc-workloads) had 27 bursts vs 0 in the previous period, 10408 log lines, 1024 nodes and 3 weeks active. It was first seen 2005-11-17 05:33:24.623263.
BGL pattern 968 daily log lines: 1008 on 2005-11-17, 0 on 2005-11-19 and 0 on 2005-11-20, then 2047 on 2005-11-24, 2045 on 2005-11-25, 3466 on 2005-11-26, 1022 on 2005-11-27 and 512 on 2005-11-28.
Apache pattern 300040 (mod_jk child workerEnv in error state; team app-integration) had 134 bursts vs 8 in the previous period (change 126), 2160 log lines and 5 weeks active.
Apache pattern 300040 weekly log lines: 19 in the week of 2005-11-07, 899 in the week of 2005-11-14, 961 in the week of 2005-11-21 and 280 in the week of 2005-11-28.
Linux pattern 700495 (Out of Memory: Killed process; team linux-ops) had 83 bursts vs 0 in the previous period, 5452 log lines on 1 node, first seen 2005-11-15 04:30:29.
Linux pattern 700495 daily log lines peaked at 1750 on 2005-11-21 (88 on 2005-11-15, 514 on 2005-11-28).
Linux httpd page allocation failure and VM: killing process httpd patterns first appeared 2005-11-21 and 2005-11-22 on 1 node; patterns 700501 and 700502 each had 11 bursts.
BGL pattern 69 (rts panic! - stopping execution; node-platform) had 33 bursts vs 27 in the previous period (change 6), 45 log lines, 33 nodes and 5 weeks active.
BGL pattern 261 (Kill job timed out. Block freed.; node-platform) had 34 bursts vs 41 in the previous period (change -7), 48 log lines and 5 weeks active.
Apache pattern 300020 (Directory index forbidden by rule) had the most bursts, 372 vs 246 in the previous period, but is judged kind 'not a problem' with p_threat 0.66.
1. BGL ciod 'Error reading message prefix on CioStream socket ... Link has been severed': new this period, widespread, with lines accelerating late in the month. Investigate first. — owner hpc-workloads — 27 bursts vs 0 previous (change 27); 10408 log lines; 1024 nodes; 3 weeks active; 3466 lines on 2005-11-26 — Check what changed around 2005-11-17 05:33 and why lines peak 2005-11-24 to 2005-11-26. Correlate with the related ciod 'Connection reset by peer' pattern 988 and the kernel termination pattern 562.
2. Apache mod_jk child workerEnv in error state: large rise in recurrences over a mostly quiet previous period. — owner app-integration — 134 bursts vs 8 previous (change 126); 2160 log lines; 5 weeks active; 899 lines in week of 2005-11-14 and 961 in week of 2005-11-21 — Review mod_jk and backend worker state from the week of 2005-11-14 onward. Check for config or deploy changes and the related jk2_init scoreboard pattern 300022 (26 bursts vs 6).
3. Linux Out of Memory kills, followed by httpd page allocation failures and process kills. — owner linux-ops — 83 bursts vs 0 previous (change 83); 5452 log lines; 1 node; 3 weeks active; peak 1750 lines on 2005-11-21 — Check memory use on the affected host since 2005-11-15 and what httpd or other workload was running around 2005-11-21, when the allocation failures began.
4. BGL kernel 'rts panic! - stopping execution' recurring across many nodes. — owner node-platform — 33 bursts vs 27 previous (change 6); 45 log lines; 33 nodes; 5 weeks active — Sample affected nodes and check whether the panics share a midplane or job. Also review the new 'invalid operation exception' patterns (14 bursts each, first seen 2005-11-17).
5. BGL 'Kill job timed out. Block freed.' recurring, but decreasing. — owner node-platform — 34 bursts vs 41 previous (change -7); 48 log lines; 5 weeks active — Keep monitoring. Confirm the decline is real and not just an effect of the new ciod errors in rank 1.
Hypothesis: The ciod link-severed errors may stem from an I/O or tree network problem that also produces the 'Connection reset by peer' errors (pattern 988, first seen 2005-11-18). Would confirm: A timeline overlap of patterns 968, 988 and 562 on the same nodes or jobs, plus I/O node health records.
Hypothesis: The Linux OOM kills may be driven by memory exhaustion on one host, with the later httpd page allocation failures and process kills as consequences. Would confirm: Host memory and swap metrics and the process list around 2005-11-15 and 2005-11-21.
Hypothesis: The rise in mod_jk errors may reflect a backend worker instability beginning in the week of 2005-11-14. Would confirm: Backend worker logs and deploy or config change history for that week.

Next step: Check memory on the Linux host with the OOM kills and httpd allocation failures. — 83 bursts vs 0 previous on a single node, peaking at 1750 lines on 2005-11-21.
Next step: Triage the BGL rts panic and new invalid operation exception patterns by node. — Pattern 69 had 33 bursts across 33 nodes; patterns 943, 944 and 945 had 14 bursts each, all new.

sql: WITH now AS ( SELECT pattern_id, count(*) AS lines, count(DISTINCT node) AS nodes, count(DISTINCT date_trunc('week', ts)) AS weeks_active, count(*) FILTER (WHERE (severity IN ('FATAL', 'FAILURE', 'SEVERE', 'ERROR', 'CRITICAL') OR severity IN ('WARN', 'WARNING') OR status >= 500 OR severity IS NULL)) AS problem_lines FROM logs WHERE dataset = 'bgl' AND ts >= '2005-11-01 00:00:00' AND ts < '2005-11-29 00:00:00' AND pattern_id IS NOT NULL GROUP BY 1 ), top_node AS ( SELECT pattern_id, max(n) AS top_node_lines FROM ( SELECT pattern_id, node, count(*) AS n FROM logs WHERE dataset = 'bgl' AND ts >= '2005-11-01 00:00:00' AND ts < '2005-11-29 00:00:00' AND node IS NOT NULL GROUP BY 1, 2) GROUP BY 1 ), b_now AS ( SELECT pattern_id, count(*) AS bursts FROM bursts WHERE dataset = 'bgl' AND start_ts >= '2005-11-01 00:00:00' AND start_ts < '2005-11-29 00:00:00' GROUP BY 1 ), b_prev AS ( SELECT pattern_id, count(*) AS bursts_prev FROM bursts WHERE dataset = 'bgl' AND start_ts >= '2005-10-04 00:00:00' AND start_ts < '2005-11-01 00:00:00' GROUP BY 1 ), base AS ( SELECT p.pattern_id, p.template, p.component, coalesce(o.team, 'unowned') AS team, p.severity, now.lines, now.problem_lines, now.nodes, now.weeks_active, coalesce(b_now.bursts, 0) AS bursts, coalesce(b_prev.bursts_prev, 0) AS bursts_prev, coalesce(b_now.bursts, 0) - coalesce(b_prev.bursts_prev, 0) AS change, round(top_node.top_node_lines::DOUBLE / now.lines, 3) AS top_node_share, p.first_ts AS first_seen, p.first_ts >= '2005-11-01 00:00:00' AS new, round(j.p_fault, 3) AS p_fault, round(j.p_dump, 3) AS p_dump, round(j.p_problem, 3) AS p_problem, round(j.p_threat, 3) AS p_threat, j.kind FROM now JOIN patterns p ON p.dataset = 'bgl' AND p.pattern_id = now.pattern_id LEFT JOIN pattern_judgments j ON j.dataset = 'bgl' AND j.pattern_id = now.pattern_id LEFT JOIN ownership o ON o.dataset = 'bgl' AND o.component = p.component LEFT JOIN top_node ON top_node.pattern_id = now.pattern_id LEFT JOIN b_now ON b_now.pattern_id = now.pattern_id LEFT JOIN b_prev ON b_prev.pattern_id = now.pattern_id WHERE TRUE AND now.problem_lines > 0 AND j.p_problem >= 0.5 ) SELECT *, count(*) OVER () AS candidates FROM base ORDER BY bursts DESC, nodes DESC, pattern_id LIMIT 20

Lines matching "machine check interrupt" peaked in the week of 2005-10-03 at 21 log lines, then held at 11 log lines for each of the next three weeks. The exact template (pattern 33) fell from 15 log lines in the week of 2005-10-03 to 7, 4 and 6. The owner is node-platform (component KERNEL).
Scope: Dataset bgl, 2005-10-01 to 2005-11-01, weekly buckets. Filters: text search "machine check interrupt" and pattern_id 33; the top-patterns ranking is limited to component KERNEL and problem-like patterns (p_problem >= 0.5) compared with 2005-08-31 to 2005-10-01. The trend results were not truncated. The top-patterns list was truncated (40 matches, 30 shown). The first and last weekly buckets are partial because of the period boundaries.
A text search for "machine check interrupt" found 61 log lines in the period. Weekly counts by bucket start: 2005-09-26: 4, 2005-10-03: 21, 2005-10-10: 11, 2005-10-17: 11, 2005-10-24: 11, 2005-10-31: 3.
The exact template 'machine check interrupt' (pattern 33) had 37 log lines in the period. Weekly counts by bucket start: 2005-09-26: 3, 2005-10-03: 15, 2005-10-10: 7, 2005-10-17: 4, 2005-10-24: 6, 2005-10-31: 2.
Pattern 33 had 34 bursts across 34 nodes, active in 6 weeks, versus 38 bursts in the previous period (change -4). Its top node accounted for a share of 0.081 of its log lines.
The ownership data lists pattern 33 under component KERNEL, team node-platform. The same team owns the related variants (patterns 86 and 93).
Variant pattern 93 ('machine check interrupt (bit=<N>): L<N> major internal error') had 10 bursts on 8 nodes versus 5 bursts in the previous period (change 5). Variant pattern 86 (L<N> dcache unit data parity error) had 14 bursts on 13 nodes versus 14 in the previous period (change 0).
1. Investigate first: 'machine check interrupt' (pattern 33, kernel hardware failure). It is the broadest of the machine-check patterns, spread across many nodes, and recurring in all 6 weeks. — owner node-platform — 34 bursts on 34 nodes, 6 weeks active, previous period 38 bursts (change -4); 37 log lines, weekly 3/15/7/4/6/2; top node share 0.081. — Check whether the 34 nodes share a rack, midplane or job mix. Confirm why the week of 2005-10-03 (15 log lines) was the peak.
2. 'machine check interrupt (bit=<N>): L<N> major internal error' (pattern 93) is the only machine-check variant that increased versus the previous period. — owner node-platform — 10 bursts on 8 nodes, 5 weeks active, previous period 5 bursts (change 5); top node share 0.2. — Review the 8 affected nodes for repeat offenders and check whether the increase is concentrated in specific weeks.
3. 'machine check interrupt (bit=<N>d): L<N> dcache unit data parity error' (pattern 86) is steady, with no improvement. — owner node-platform — 14 bursts on 13 nodes, 5 weeks active, previous period 14 bursts (change 0). — Decide whether the unchanged recurrence warrants hardware triage of the affected nodes.
Hypothesis: The week of 2005-10-03 peak may reflect a cluster of hardware faults early in the month rather than a sustained rise, since later weeks are lower. Would confirm: Examine the bursts in that week for shared nodes, racks or times, and check the BG/L maintenance records.

Would confirm: List the pattern_ids of the text-search matches within the period and reconcile them against pattern 33.

The ranked patterns use the period 2017-04-19 12:02 → 2017-05-17 12:02 against the previous period 2017-03-22 12:02 → 2017-04-19 12:02. 'Bad response code while validating token' is ERROR with 2 log lines and 2 bursts. 'Unable to validate token: Failed to fetch token data from identity server' is CRITICAL with 2 log lines and 2 bursts.
The largest 404 pattern shown is 'GET /openstack/<N>/user_data' with status 404: 1905 log lines, 3 bursts, 2 weeks active, bursts_prev 0. It is judged kind 'not a problem' with p_problem 0.16.
1. old.text:
Several recurring patterns had more bursts in October 2005 than in the previous window. The biggest is BGL "Kill job <N> timed out. Block freed." (44 bursts vs 29, owner node-platform). Other BGL KERNEL hardware-error patterns (also node-platform) and Linux ssh authentication failures (owner linux-ops) also rose.
Scope: Datasets bgl, apache and linux. Period 2005-10-01 to 2005-11-01, compared with the previous window 2005-08-31 to 2005-10-01, which is not exactly September. Filters: problem patterns only, ranked by growth in bursts. Each dataset's top_patterns result is truncated to 10 rows (bgl 86 matches, apache 20, linux 36), so lower-growth patterns are not shown.
BGL pattern 261 "Kill job <N> timed out. Block freed." (KERNEL, FATAL, owner node-platform) had 44 bursts in October vs 29 in the previous window (change 15), over 47 log lines and 6 weeks active.
Weekly log lines for pattern 261 were 6 (week of 2005-10-03), 7 (2005-10-10), 20 (2005-10-17), 10 (2005-10-24) and 2 (2005-10-31). Earlier weeks were 8, 10, 2, 4 and 8.
Pattern 261 log lines ran from 2005-10-01 05:21:34.993680 to 2005-10-31 21:12:25.762602. The result reports 0 distinct nodes, so spread is unknown.
BGL pattern 93 "machine check interrupt (bit=<N>): L<N> major internal error" (owner node-platform) had 10 bursts vs 5 (change 5) across 8 nodes and 5 weeks active.
BGL patterns 120, 122, 123, 124, 125, 126, 135 and 153 (all KERNEL, FATAL, node-platform) each went from 2 bursts to 4 (change 2), each on 4 nodes and 4 weeks active. All were first seen on 2005-06-08 between 04:48:52 and 04:48:58.
Linux pattern 700272 (sshd(pam_unix) authentication failure, user=test, owner linux-ops) had 14 bursts vs 1 (change 13) over 88 log lines, all on 1 node, 3 weeks active. Pattern 700267 (same family) had 14 bursts vs 7 (change 7) over 126 log lines, 4 weeks active.
Apache pattern 300046 "script not found or unable to stat" (mod_jk, owner app-integration) is new in October: first seen 2005-10-24 13:03:50, 1 burst vs 0, 17 log lines. Pattern 300040 (mod_jk workerEnv in error state) went from 7 bursts to 8.
1. BGL "Kill job <N> timed out. Block freed." (job kill timeouts, KERNEL FATAL). Investigate first: largest growth in bursts among the BGL patterns and active in 6 weeks. — owner node-platform — 44 bursts vs 29 (change 15); 47 log lines; 6 weeks active; 20 log lines in the week of 2005-10-17 vs 6 and 7 in the two weeks before. — Check what happened around the week of 2005-10-17 and whether the job kill timeouts cluster on particular blocks or jobs.
2. BGL machine check interrupt: L<N> major internal error (hardware failure, KERNEL FATAL). — owner node-platform — 10 bursts vs 5 (change 5); 8 nodes; 5 weeks active. — Review the 8 affected nodes for hardware faults and decide on repair or removal from service.
3. BGL group of 8 KERNEL FATAL memory and parity error patterns (uncorrectable errors, parity errors, EDRAM, DDR, directory), each recurring twice as often. — owner node-platform — Each of patterns 120, 122, 123, 124, 125, 126, 135 and 153: 4 bursts vs 2 (change 2), 4 nodes, 4 weeks active. — Check whether the 8 patterns occur together on the same 4 nodes and treat them as one fault investigation.
4. Linux sshd authentication failures (pam_unix, ssh) rising, including a test-user pattern. — owner linux-ops — Pattern 700272: 14 bursts vs 1 (change 13), 88 log lines, 3 weeks active. Pattern 700267: 14 bursts vs 7 (change 7), 126 log lines, 4 weeks active. Both on 1 node. — Review the source hosts of the failed ssh logins and decide whether blocking or rate limiting is needed.
5. Apache mod_jk errors: new "script not found or unable to stat" pattern and a recurring workerEnv error-state pattern. — owner app-integration — Pattern 300046: new, first seen 2005-10-24 13:03:50, 1 burst vs 0, 17 log lines. Pattern 300040: 8 bursts vs 7 (change 1), 28 log lines, 4 weeks active. — Check the mod_jk configuration and worker mapping changes around 2005-10-24.
Hypothesis: The 8 BGL memory and parity patterns share a first-seen time within seconds on 2005-06-08 and the same burst counts, which may mean one underlying hardware event is producing all of them. Would confirm: Compare timestamps and nodes across the 8 patterns to see whether they co-occur in the same bursts.
Hypothesis: The rise in ssh authentication failures from a single node may reflect repeated login attempts (for example password guessing) from outside hosts. Would confirm: Count failures per rhost and user over time, and check for successful logins following the failures.
Unknown: Root cause of any of these patterns is not established by the logs.
Unknown: Spread of BGL pattern 261 across nodes is unknown (0 nodes reported), and apache logs carry no node or host.
Unknown: The comparison window starts 2005-08-31, so it is not exactly September.
Unknown: Customer impact, downtime and cost are not in the logs.
Unknown: The Linux ssh patterns are labelled kind "not a problem" with p_threat 0.97 by the judgment table, so whether they are an operational problem or a security signal is unclear.
Unknown: Results are truncated to the top 10 by growth per dataset, so other worsening patterns may exist.
Next step: Pull burst timestamps and block/job details for pattern 261 for the week of 2005-10-17 and compare with the earlier weeks. — It has the largest burst growth (44 vs 29), with 20 log lines in the week of 2005-10-17.
Next step: Check the nodes reporting pattern 93 and the 8 memory/parity patterns for co-occurrence and hardware health. — Bursts doubled (5 to 10 and 2 to 4) on 8 and 4 nodes respectively.
Next step: Break down pattern 700272 and 700267 failures by source host and user. — Bursts rose 1 to 14 and 7 to 14 on a single node.
Next step: Review mod_jk configuration changes around 2005-10-24. — Pattern 300046 appeared as new on 2005-10-24 13:03:50 with 17 log lines.

For October 2005 the strongest priority is the Blue Gene/L (bgl) hardware-fault family owned by node-platform: DDR, EDRAM and machine-check errors. Node-platform also holds the most problem bursts and grew from the previous period. Apache and Linux problem bursts fell over the month.
Scope: Datasets bgl, apache and linux, 2005-10-01 to 2005-11-01, with the previous period 2005-08-31 to 2005-10-01 for comparison. Filters: problem patterns only (jev filter, p_problem >= 0.5). Priority tables are truncated to the top 10 of 86 (bgl), 20 (apache) and 36 (linux) candidates. The weekly trend tables are not truncated. The ranking below is the bgl computed order.
bgl team roll-up: node-platform has 43 problem patterns and 251 bursts (previous 217, change 34). cluster-control has 10 problem patterns and 51 bursts (previous 56, change -5). hpc-workloads has 33 problem patterns and 43 bursts (previous 18, change 25).
bgl weekly problem bursts total 345 in the period and the trend reading is 'no clear change'.
The bgl pattern 'Kill job <N> timed out. Block freed.' (node-platform) has the largest growth in bursts: 44 bursts versus 29 previously (change 15), active in 6 weeks.
apache team roll-up: web-platform has 17 problem patterns and 358 bursts (previous 487, change -129). app-integration has 3 problem patterns and 16 bursts (previous 21, change -5). The weekly trend reading is 'improving' with 374 bursts in total.
linux team roll-up: linux-ops has 36 problem patterns and 111 bursts (previous 85, change 26). The weekly trend reading is 'improving'. The top-ranked linux patterns are sshd authentication failures that the judgment labels 'not a problem'.
1. Kernel reports an uncorrectable error in external DDR memory (hardware failure judgment). — owner node-platform — 4 bursts (previous 2, change 2) on 4 nodes, active in 4 weeks; score 82.1. — Decide whether to fund a hardware inspection or replacement review of the affected nodes' memory.
2. Kernel reports an uncorrectable error in an EDRAM bank (hardware failure judgment). — owner node-platform — 4 bursts (previous 2, change 2) on 4 nodes, active in 4 weeks; score 81.6. — Handle together with rank 1. Ask node-platform to confirm whether the same nodes are affected and to report back.
3. Machine check interrupt, L<N> major internal error (hardware failure judgment). — owner node-platform — 10 bursts (previous 5, change 5) on 8 nodes, active in 5 weeks; score 80.2. — Decide on node-platform capacity for a wider node health review, since this pattern touches the most nodes of the top three.
Hypothesis: The DDR, EDRAM and parity error patterns share the same count (4 bursts) and the same 4 nodes, which may indicate one recurring underlying hardware event rather than independent faults. Would confirm: Compare the node locations and timestamps of these patterns, and check hardware service records for the same node cards.
Hypothesis: The growth in 'Kill job timed out' bursts may reflect workload or scheduling pressure rather than hardware. Would confirm: Correlate these bursts with job submissions and with the hpc-workloads team's pattern growth.
Unknown: Cost, downtime and customer impact are not in these logs.
Unknown: Root cause is not established by these logs.
Unknown: Priority scores are relative within each dataset, so bgl, apache and linux scores are not directly comparable across datasets.
Unknown: The priority tables show only the top 10 candidates per dataset, so lower-ranked patterns are not shown.
Next step: Open a hardware review of the DDR, EDRAM and machine-check nodes and report which nodes recur. — The top three bgl patterns are all hardware-fault judgments owned by node-platform, which has 251 bursts (change 34).
Next step: Review the 'Kill job timed out' growth together with hpc-workloads' growth of 25 bursts. — 'Kill job timed out' had the largest burst growth (change 15), and hpc-workloads' bursts rose from 18 to 43.
Next step: Make no new investment in apache now. Confirm the downward trend continues next month. — web-platform bursts changed by -129 and the weekly reading is 'improving'.

ev-33c966f713.note: lines = log entries; bursts = recurrences of one pattern split by > 30 min quiet; components lists at most 12 (components_total = all); a NULL *_meaning = field not logged; severities empty = the format has no log level.

rows.title: Blue Gene/L supercomputer RAS logs (LLNL)
rows.description: Loghub BGL: reliability/availability/serviceability events of the Blue Gene/L supercomputer, 2005-06-03 to 2006-01-04 (214 days). Location = rack/midplane/node (R02-M1-N0-C:J12-U11: rack R02, midplane M1, node card N0, C = compute / I = I/O card). Components KERNEL, APP, MMCS, ... Alert labels exist for evaluation only.
rows.node_meaning: compute / I/O node: rack-midplane-nodecard-card-unit (C = compute card, I = I/O card)
rows.location_meaning: rack/midplane/node (first level = a whole rack, two levels = a midplane)

rows.title: OpenStack nova logs (cloud VM lifecycle and API)
rows.description: Loghub OpenStack: nova-api / nova-compute / nova-scheduler logs of a small cloud, 2017-05-16 to 2017-05-17, with request ids, tenant ids, VM instance ids, HTTP status and request latency inline. Some VMs had injected anomalies (labels for evaluation only).
rows.request_meaning: nova request id (req-…): one API call and the work it triggers
rows.object_meaning: VM instance uuid: follows one VM across requests and services (spawn, build, delete)
rows.status_meaning: HTTP status of nova-api requests (status: N in the message)
rows.duration_meaning: HTTP request time (time: N) and VM lifecycle step times (Took N seconds to spawn / build / delete)

rows.title: Zookeeper coordination service logs (one ensemble member)
rows.description: Loghub Zookeeper: Java log4j lines from a ZooKeeper ensemble member, 2015-07-29 to 2015-08-27. component = Java class, location = class/thread. Leader election, quorum connections, client sessions.
rows.location_meaning: Java class/thread, e.g. QuorumCnxManager/QuorumPeer[myid=1]_0.0.0.0_2181 (filter one class with its name alone)

rows.title: Apache httpd error log (one web server)
rows.description: Loghub Apache: error_log of one Apache httpd server, 2005-06-09 to 2006-02-28 (264 days). Levels notice / warn / error; client IPs inside messages are extracted as entities (ip:...). Multi-line messages inherit the previous line time and level.

rows.title: OpenSSH server auth log (host LabSZ)
rows.description: Loghub OpenSSH: sshd auth log of one internet-facing server (LabSZ), 28 days from Dec 10 (year not logged: Dec = 2017, Jan = 2018 assumed). No log levels (severity is NULL). Failed passwords, invalid users, break-in attempts; attacker IPs are entities (ip:...); request_id = sshd-<pid> = one connection.
rows.node_meaning: host name of the server (one host: LabSZ)
rows.request_meaning: sshd-<pid>: one SSH connection (process ids are reused over the 28 days, so one id can hold several sessions; request_timeline splits them)

rows.title: HDFS_v1 Hadoop file system logs (scale test, 11M lines)
rows.description: Loghub HDFS_v1: HDFS NameNode / DataNode logs of a Hadoop cluster over about 39 hours from 2008-11-09. request_id = the HDFS block id (blk_...), which follows one block across replicas; client and datanode IPs inside messages are entities (ip:...). Block-level anomaly labels exist for evaluation only.
rows.request_meaning: HDFS block id (blk_…): the whole life of one block across datanodes (allocate, receive, replicate, delete)

rows.title: OpenTelemetry demo app logs (slice of 1 B remote records)
rows.description: OpenTelemetry demo (microservices webshop on Kubernetes) logs from the public text_bench Parquet on S3 (part_000 = 1 billion records, first 30 minutes of 2025-09-23). This dataset holds 0.1 s of every minute of those 30 minutes; the full files are queried in place with the remote_* tools. component = service, location = namespace/node/pod, request_id = TraceId.
rows.node_meaning: Kubernetes node name
rows.request_meaning: OpenTelemetry TraceId (32 hex chars): one user request across services

rows.title: Linux syslog of one server (host combo)
rows.description: Loghub Linux: /var/log/messages of one Linux server (combo), Jun 9 to Feb 28 (year not logged: Jun-Dec = 2005, Jan-Feb = 2006 assumed). No log levels (severity is NULL). Kernel, sshd / ftpd / su authentication, udev, cron, named.
rows.node_meaning: host name (one host: combo)
rows.request_meaning: <program>-<pid>: one process (pids are reused over months; request_timeline splits sessions at quiet gaps)

rows.title: HealthApp Android app log (step counter and health data sync)
rows.description: Loghub HealthApp: log of an Android health app, 2017-12-23 to 2018-01-03 (dates not zero-padded in the raw file). No log levels (severity is NULL), no host. Components are app modules: Step_* = step counting, HiH_* = HiHealth data store and sync.
rows.request_meaning: app process id: all lines of one app process

sql: WITH now AS ( SELECT pattern_id, count(*) AS lines, count(DISTINCT node) AS nodes, count(DISTINCT date_trunc('week', ts)) AS weeks_active, count(*) FILTER (WHERE (severity IN ('FATAL', 'FAILURE', 'SEVERE', 'ERROR', 'CRITICAL') OR severity IN ('WARN', 'WARNING') OR status >= 500 OR severity IS NULL)) AS problem_lines FROM logs WHERE dataset = 'bgl' AND ts >= '2005-10-01 00:00:00' AND ts < '2005-11-01 00:00:00' AND pattern_id IS NOT NULL GROUP BY 1 ), top_node AS ( SELECT pattern_id, max(n) AS top_node_lines FROM ( SELECT pattern_id, node, count(*) AS n FROM logs WHERE dataset = 'bgl' AND ts >= '2005-10-01 00:00:00' AND ts < '2005-11-01 00:00:00' AND node IS NOT NULL GROUP BY 1, 2) GROUP BY 1 ), b_now AS ( SELECT pattern_id, count(*) AS bursts FROM bursts WHERE dataset = 'bgl' AND start_ts >= '2005-10-01 00:00:00' AND start_ts < '2005-11-01 00:00:00' GROUP BY 1 ), b_prev AS ( SELECT pattern_id, count(*) AS bursts_prev FROM bursts WHERE dataset = 'bgl' AND start_ts >= '2005-08-31 00:00:00' AND start_ts < '2005-10-01 00:00:00' GROUP BY 1 ), base AS ( SELECT p.pattern_id, p.template, p.component, coalesce(o.team, 'unowned') AS team, p.severity, now.lines, now.problem_lines, now.nodes, now.weeks_active, coalesce(b_now.bursts, 0) AS bursts, coalesce(b_prev.bursts_prev, 0) AS bursts_prev, coalesce(b_now.bursts, 0) - coalesce(b_prev.bursts_prev, 0) AS change, round(top_node.top_node_lines::DOUBLE / now.lines, 3) AS top_node_share, p.first_ts AS first_seen, p.first_ts >= '2005-10-01 00:00:00' AS new, round(j.p_fault, 3) AS p_fault, round(j.p_dump, 3) AS p_dump, round(j.p_problem, 3) AS p_problem, round(j.p_threat, 3) AS p_threat, j.kind FROM now JOIN patterns p ON p.dataset = 'bgl' AND p.pattern_id = now.pattern_id LEFT JOIN pattern_judgments j ON j.dataset = 'bgl' AND j.pattern_id = now.pattern_id LEFT JOIN ownership o ON o.dataset = 'bgl' AND o.component = p.component LEFT JOIN top_node ON top_node.pattern_id = now.pattern_id LEFT JOIN b_now ON b_now.pattern_id = now.pattern_id LEFT JOIN b_prev ON b_prev.pattern_id = now.pattern_id WHERE TRUE AND now.problem_lines > 0 AND j.p_problem >= 0.5 ), inputs AS ( SELECT *, round(weeks_active::DOUBLE / 6, 3) AS persistence, round(problem_lines::DOUBLE / lines, 3) AS problem_share, p_problem AS severity_input FROM base ), ranked AS ( SELECT *, cume_dist() OVER (ORDER BY bursts) AS pr_frequency, cume_dist() OVER (ORDER BY change) AS pr_trend, cume_dist() OVER (ORDER BY nodes) AS pr_spread, cume_dist() OVER (ORDER BY persistence) AS pr_persistence, cume_dist() OVER (ORDER BY severity_input) AS pr_severity FROM inputs ) SELECT *, round(100 * (0.3 * pr_frequency + 0.2 * pr_trend + 0.25 * pr_spread + 0.15 * pr_persistence + 0.1 * pr_severity), 1) AS score FROM ranked ORDER BY score DESC, bursts DESC, pattern_id

sql: SELECT s.b AS bucket_start, count(x.t) AS bursts FROM generate_series(date_trunc('week', TIMESTAMP '2005-10-01 00:00:00'), TIMESTAMP '2005-11-01 00:00:00', interval '7 days') s(b) LEFT JOIN (SELECT b.start_ts AS t FROM bursts b JOIN patterns p ON p.dataset = b.dataset AND p.pattern_id = b.pattern_id LEFT JOIN ownership o ON o.dataset = p.dataset AND o.component = p.component LEFT JOIN pattern_judgments j ON j.dataset = p.dataset AND j.pattern_id = p.pattern_id WHERE TRUE AND j.p_problem >= 0.5 AND p.problem_lines > 0 AND b.dataset = 'bgl' AND b.start_ts >= '2005-10-01 00:00:00' AND b.start_ts < '2005-11-01 00:00:00') x ON date_trunc('week', x.t) = s.b GROUP BY 1 ORDER BY 1

SELECT round(regr_slope(bursts, i), 3) AS slope, round(avg(bursts) FILTER (WHERE i < 6 / 2.0), 2) AS first_half_mean, round(avg(bursts) FILTER (WHERE i >= 6 / 2.0), 2) AS second_half_mean, sum(bursts) AS total FROM (SELECT row_number() OVER (ORDER BY bucket_start) - 1 AS i, bursts FROM (SELECT s.b AS bucket_start, count(x.t) AS bursts FROM generate_series(date_trunc('week', TIMESTAMP '2005-10-01 00:00:00'), TIMESTAMP '2005-11-01 00:00:00', interval '7 days') s(b) LEFT JOIN (SELECT b.start_ts AS t FROM bursts b JOIN patterns p ON p.dataset = b.dataset AND p.pattern_id = b.pattern_id LEFT JOIN ownership o ON o.dataset = p.dataset AND o.component = p.component LEFT JOIN pattern_judgments j ON j.dataset = p.dataset AND j.pattern_id = p.pattern_id WHERE TRUE AND j.p_problem >= 0.5 AND p.problem_lines > 0 AND b.dataset = 'bgl' AND b.start_ts >= '2005-10-01 00:00:00' AND b.start_ts < '2005-11-01 00:00:00') x ON date_trunc('week', x.t) = s.b GROUP BY 1 ORDER BY 1))

SELECT team, round(regr_slope(n, i), 3) AS slope, sum(n) AS bursts FROM (SELECT t.team, s.i, count(x.t) AS n FROM (SELECT row_number() OVER (ORDER BY b) - 1 AS i, b FROM generate_series(date_trunc('week', TIMESTAMP '2005-10-01 00:00:00'), TIMESTAMP '2005-11-01 00:00:00', interval '7 days') s(b)) s CROSS JOIN (SELECT DISTINCT coalesce(o.team, 'unowned') AS team FROM bursts b JOIN patterns p ON p.dataset = b.dataset AND p.pattern_id = b.pattern_id LEFT JOIN ownership o ON o.dataset = p.dataset AND o.component = p.component LEFT JOIN pattern_judgments j ON j.dataset = p.dataset AND j.pattern_id = p.pattern_id WHERE TRUE AND j.p_problem >= 0.5 AND p.problem_lines > 0 AND b.dataset = 'bgl' AND b.start_ts >= '2005-10-01 00:00:00' AND b.start_ts < '2005-11-01 00:00:00') t LEFT JOIN (SELECT b.start_ts AS t, coalesce(o.team, 'unowned') AS team FROM bursts b JOIN patterns p ON p.dataset = b.dataset AND p.pattern_id = b.pattern_id LEFT JOIN ownership o ON o.dataset = p.dataset AND o.component = p.component LEFT JOIN pattern_judgments j ON j.dataset = p.dataset AND j.pattern_id = p.pattern_id WHERE TRUE AND j.p_problem >= 0.5 AND p.problem_lines > 0 AND b.dataset = 'bgl' AND b.start_ts >= '2005-10-01 00:00:00' AND b.start_ts < '2005-11-01 00:00:00') x ON date_trunc('week', x.t) = s.b AND x.team = t.team GROUP BY 1, 2) GROUP BY 1 ORDER BY bursts DESC

Three problems lead, one per dataset: repeated ssh authentication failures (linux-ops), recurring worker.jni startup errors (web-platform), and uncorrectable memory errors on BGL nodes (node-platform). The BGL item is the one judged a hardware fault; the linux item is judged 'not a problem' by the pattern judgment, so it needs a security-versus-noise decision rather than a repair.
Scope: Datasets bgl, apache and linux, 2005-10-01 to 2005-11-01, compared with 2005-08-31 to 2005-10-01. Filter: problem patterns only. Each table is truncated to its top 5 (86, 20 and 36 matching patterns). Scores are relative within each dataset, so the cross-dataset order below is by score and is indicative only.
node-platform (bgl) has 43 problem patterns, 251 bursts (217 in the previous period, change 34) and 4150 log lines.
hpc-workloads (bgl) has 33 problem patterns, 43 bursts (18 previously, change 25) and 36295 log lines. cluster-control (bgl) has 10 problem patterns and 51 bursts (56 previously, change -5).
web-platform (apache) has 17 problem patterns and 358 bursts (487 previously, change -129). app-integration has 3 problem patterns and 16 bursts (21 previously, change -5).
linux-ops (linux) has 36 problem patterns, 111 bursts (85 previously, change 26) and 514 log lines.
The top bgl pattern, 'uncorrectable error detected in external DDR', was judged a hardware failure (p_fault 0.96). It had 4 bursts (2 previously) across 4 nodes and was active in 4 weeks.
The bgl pattern 'machine check interrupt (bit=<N>): L<N> major internal error' had 10 bursts (5 previously) across 8 nodes and was active in 5 weeks.
The top apache pattern, 'config.update(): Can't create worker.jni:onStartup', had 6 bursts (6 previously, change 0) and was active in 5 weeks. Apache logs carry no node, so spread is unknown.
The top linux pattern, an sshd(pam_unix) authentication failure for user=test, had 14 bursts (1 previously, change 13) and 88 log lines, all on 1 node. Its judgment kind is 'not a problem' (p_fault 0.18).
1. Repeated ssh authentication failures for user 'test' (sshd(pam_unix)), on a single node. The pattern judgment labels it 'not a problem', but the burst count rose sharply. — owner linux-ops — Score 96.5; 14 bursts vs 1 previously (change 13); 88 log lines; 1 node; active in 3 weeks. — Decide whether this is a security matter or noise: ask linux-ops to review the source of the failures and confirm whether access controls need tightening.
2. Recurring web application startup errors: config.update() cannot create worker.jni:onStartup. Several sibling patterns show the same burst counts. — owner web-platform — Score 91.0; 6 bursts vs 6 previously (change 0); 6 log lines; active in 5 weeks; spread unknown (nodes 0). — Decide whether to fund a fix for the persistent worker.jni startup configuration errors; the team's total bursts fell (358 vs 487).
3. Uncorrectable memory errors (external DDR) on BGL nodes, judged a hardware failure. Related machine check interrupts affect 8 nodes. — owner node-platform — Score 82.1; 4 bursts vs 2 previously (change 2); 4 nodes; active in 4 weeks. Team total 251 bursts vs 217 (change 34). — Ask node-platform to confirm which nodes are affected and decide on hardware diagnostics or replacement.
Hypothesis: The linux authentication failures may be external password-guessing against ssh, since the templates include remote host names. Would confirm: Check source addresses and timing of the failed logins, and whether any later login succeeded.
Hypothesis: The BGL uncorrectable DDR, EDRAM and directory errors may come from failing memory hardware on a few nodes. Would confirm: Run hardware diagnostics on the affected nodes and check whether the same nodes repeat across bursts.
Hypothesis: The worker.jni errors may come from a persistent mod_jk or worker configuration fault that recurs at each start. Would confirm: Review the worker configuration and compare burst times with restarts.
Unknown: Cost, downtime and customer impact are not in these logs.
Unknown: Root cause is not established by these logs.
Unknown: Whether any ssh authentication attempt succeeded is not shown.
Unknown: Apache logs carry no node, so how widely the errors spread is unknown.
Unknown: Only the top 5 per dataset are shown, so lower-ranked patterns are not reviewed here.
Next step: Review the sources of the ssh authentication failures and decide whether to block or alert on them. — Bursts rose from 1 to 14 on one node, but the pattern judgment says 'not a problem'; a human decision is needed.
Next step: Run hardware diagnostics on the nodes reporting uncorrectable errors and machine check interrupts. — These patterns are judged hardware failures (p_fault 0.96) and span 4 and 8 nodes respectively.
Next step: Review the worker.jni startup configuration and decide whether to fund a fix. — The top patterns persisted across 5 weeks at 6 bursts each, with no change from the previous period.

coalesce(b_prev.bursts_prev, 0) AS change, round(top_node.top_node_lines::DOUBLE / now.lines, 3) AS top_node_share, p.first_ts AS first_seen, p.first_ts >= '2005-10-01 00:00:00' AS new, round(j.p_fault, 3) AS p_fault, round(j.p_dump, 3) AS p_dump, round(j.p_problem, 3) AS p_problem, round(j.p_threat, 3) AS p_threat, j.kind FROM now JOIN patterns p ON p.dataset = 'bgl' AND p.pattern_id = now.pattern_id LEFT JOIN pattern_judgments j ON j.dataset = 'bgl' AND j.pattern_id = now.pattern_id LEFT JOIN ownership o ON o.dataset = 'bgl' AND o.component = p.component LEFT JOIN top_node ON top_node.pattern_id = now.pattern_id LEFT JOIN b_now ON b_now.pattern_id = now.pattern_id LEFT JOIN b_prev ON b_prev.pattern_id = now.pattern_id WHERE TRUE AND now.problem_lines > 0 AND j.p_problem >= 0.5 ), inputs AS ( SELECT *, round(weeks_active::DOUBLE / 6, 3) AS persistence, round(problem_lines::DOUBLE / lines, 3) AS problem_share, p_problem AS severity_input FROM base ), ranked AS ( SELECT *, cume_dist() OVER (ORDER BY bursts) AS pr_frequency, cume_dist() OVER (ORDER BY change) AS pr_trend, cume_dist() OVER (ORDER BY nodes) AS pr_spread, cume_dist() OVER (ORDER BY persistence) AS pr_persistence, cume_dist() OVER (ORDER BY severity_input) AS pr_severity FROM inputs ) SELECT *, round(100 * (0.3 * pr_frequency + 0.2 * pr_trend + 0.25 * pr_spread + 0.15 * pr_persistence + 0.1 * pr_severity), 1) AS score FROM ranked ORDER BY score DESC, bursts DESC, pattern_id

coalesce(b_prev.bursts_prev, 0) AS change, round(top_node.top_node_lines::DOUBLE / now.lines, 3) AS top_node_share, p.first_ts AS first_seen, p.first_ts >= '2005-10-01 00:00:00' AS new, round(j.p_fault, 3) AS p_fault, round(j.p_dump, 3) AS p_dump, round(j.p_problem, 3) AS p_problem, round(j.p_threat, 3) AS p_threat, j.kind FROM now JOIN patterns p ON p.dataset = 'linux' AND p.pattern_id = now.pattern_id LEFT JOIN pattern_judgments j ON j.dataset = 'linux' AND j.pattern_id = now.pattern_id LEFT JOIN ownership o ON o.dataset = 'linux' AND o.component = p.component LEFT JOIN top_node ON top_node.pattern_id = now.pattern_id LEFT JOIN b_now ON b_now.pattern_id = now.pattern_id LEFT JOIN b_prev ON b_prev.pattern_id = now.pattern_id WHERE TRUE AND now.problem_lines > 0 AND j.p_problem >= 0.5 ), inputs AS ( SELECT *, round(weeks_active::DOUBLE / 6, 3) AS persistence, round(problem_lines::DOUBLE / lines, 3) AS problem_share, p_problem AS severity_input FROM base ), ranked AS ( SELECT *, cume_dist() OVER (ORDER BY bursts) AS pr_frequency, cume_dist() OVER (ORDER BY change) AS pr_trend, cume_dist() OVER (ORDER BY nodes) AS pr_spread, cume_dist() OVER (ORDER BY persistence) AS pr_persistence, cume_dist() OVER (ORDER BY severity_input) AS pr_severity FROM inputs ) SELECT *, round(100 * (0.3 * pr_frequency + 0.2 * pr_trend + 0.25 * pr_spread + 0.15 * pr_persistence + 0.1 * pr_severity), 1) AS score FROM ranked ORDER BY score DESC, bursts DESC, pattern_id

In these logs, node-platform (BGL) carried the most risk in September 2005: it holds ranks 1 and 2 (scores 98.4 and 95.9). Its overall bursts are about flat (268 vs 275), but its top item, the Lustre mount failure, rose from 2 to 40 bursts, and hpc-workloads is worsening fastest (106 vs 23 bursts).
Scope: Datasets bgl, apache and linux, 2005-09-01 to 2005-10-01, compared with 2005-08-02 to 2005-09-01. Candidates are problem patterns (jev filter, p_problem >= 0.5). Top-10 tables are truncated (146 bgl, 19 apache, 30 linux matches), but the team roll-ups cover all matching patterns. Scores are ranked within each dataset, so they are not strictly comparable across datasets.
node-platform (bgl): 45 problem patterns, 268 bursts vs 275 in the previous period (change -7), 26763 log lines.
hpc-workloads (bgl): 88 problem patterns, 106 bursts vs 23 in the previous period (change 83), 52757 log lines.
cluster-control (bgl): 13 problem patterns, 72 bursts vs 107 in the previous period (change -35), 72340 log lines.
web-platform (apache): 17 problem patterns, 471 bursts vs 504 (change -33), 1005 log lines. app-integration (apache): 21 bursts vs 20 (change 1).
linux-ops (linux): 30 problem patterns, 97 bursts vs 64 (change 33), 507 log lines. Its top item (score 99.0) is an ssh authentication failure pattern that the judgment labels 'not a problem'.
1. Lustre mount FAILED on bglio nodes (network or I/O failure) — owner node-platform — Score 98.4; 40 bursts vs 2 in the previous period (change 38); 1024 nodes; active 3 weeks; 23505 log lines. — Decide whether to fund a storage/I/O investigation now, since this pattern jumped from 2 to 40 bursts across 1024 nodes.
2. rts panic - stopping execution (system software failure) — owner node-platform — Score 95.9; 49 bursts vs 24 (change 25); 279 nodes; active 5 weeks; 478 log lines. — Ask the owner for a fix-or-accept decision, as the pattern was active in all 5 weeks and its bursts roughly doubled.
3. ciod: link severed on CioStream socket (network or I/O failure) — owner hpc-workloads — Score 93.9; 14 bursts vs 13 (change 1); 1024 nodes; active 4 weeks; 7152 log lines. The team overall rose from 23 to 106 bursts. — Decide on a review of the hpc-workloads rise, which is the largest team-level increase in the bgl data.
Hypothesis: The hpc-workloads rise may come partly from new 'invalid or missing program image' job-load errors (several new patterns, each seen in 1 burst across roughly 1000 nodes). Would confirm: Check whether the new load-error patterns map to a few job submissions with bad paths, and whether they recur after September.
Hypothesis: The Lustre mount failures may point to a shared filesystem or I/O-network problem rather than a node-by-node fault, since they are spread over 1024 nodes with very low top-node share. Would confirm: Compare timing of bursts against I/O-node and storage events, and check whether one filesystem or bglio node group is involved.

new.text:
Fix the new BGL kernel failure "rts: kernel terminated for reason <N>" (node-platform). It has the top priority score (96.0), appeared in August with 13 bursts and none in July, and touched 2666 nodes.
Scope: Datasets bgl, apache and linux, 2005-08-01 to 2005-09-01 (5 weeks), compared with 2005-07-01 to 2005-08-01. Filter: problem patterns only (jev filter). The priority tables are truncated to the top 5 of 148 (bgl), 18 (apache) and 21 (linux) candidates. The node-platform team table is also truncated, with 99 patterns in its roll-up. The weekly trend is not truncated. Scores are ranked within each dataset, so they are not strictly comparable across datasets.
bgl rank 1 is "rts: kernel terminated for reason <N>" (KERNEL, node-platform), score 96.0, new this period: 13 bursts vs 0 the month before, 2666 nodes, 11349 log lines, active in 3 weeks.
Team roll-up for bgl: node-platform has 99 problem patterns, 460 bursts (136 before, change 324). cluster-control has 27 patterns, 149 bursts (46 before, change 103). hpc-workloads has 22 patterns, 44 bursts (1 before, change 43).
Weekly bgl problem bursts fell from 209 (week of 2005-08-01) to 41 (week of 2005-08-29); total 653, slope -42.8, reading "improving".
Top items in the other datasets score slightly lower. apache: File does not exist (web-platform), score 95.6, 18 bursts. linux: sshd authentication failure (linux-ops), score 95.2, 22 bursts.
1. Kernel terminated for reason <N>: a new system-software failure pattern on BGL compute nodes — owner node-platform — Score 96.0; 13 bursts vs 0 before (change 13); 2666 nodes; 3 weeks active; 11349 log lines — Decide to make this the single funded fix. Ask node-platform to find what changed in August and whether it can be rolled back or patched.
2. Node card is not fully functional: a hardware failure pattern that persists across all weeks — owner cluster-control — Score 91.5; 37 bursts vs 21 before (change 16); 1967 nodes; 5 weeks active — Decide whether to fund hardware triage of the affected node cards after the first fix.
3. Can not get assembly information for node card: a hardware failure pattern that follows the same course as rank 2 — owner cluster-control — Score 90.8; 36 bursts vs 21 before (change 15); 1966 nodes; 5 weeks active — Treat it together with rank 2 and ask cluster-control whether it is the same underlying problem.
Hypothesis: The kernel termination pattern may be tied to a change introduced in August, since it was absent in July. It may also be linked to the other new KERNEL patterns (bad message headers, Lustre mount failures). Would confirm: Compare node-platform change, deploy and firmware records with the first-seen time of the pattern. Check whether the affected nodes share a software version.
Unknown: Cost, downtime and customer impact are not in these logs.

sql: WITH now AS ( SELECT pattern_id, count(*) AS lines, count(DISTINCT node) AS nodes, count(DISTINCT date_trunc('week', ts)) AS weeks_active, count(*) FILTER (WHERE (severity IN ('FATAL', 'FAILURE', 'SEVERE', 'ERROR', 'CRITICAL') OR severity IN ('WARN', 'WARNING') OR status >= 500 OR severity IS NULL)) AS problem_lines FROM logs WHERE dataset = 'bgl' AND ts >= '2005-08-01 00:00:00' AND ts < '2005-09-01 00:00:00' AND pattern_id IS NOT NULL GROUP BY 1 ), top_node AS ( SELECT pattern_id, max(n) AS top_node_lines FROM ( SELECT pattern_id, node, count(*) AS n FROM logs WHERE dataset = 'bgl' AND ts >= '2005-08-01 00:00:00' AND ts < '2005-09-01 00:00:00' AND node IS NOT NULL GROUP BY 1, 2) GROUP BY 1 ), b_now AS ( SELECT pattern_id, count(*) AS bursts FROM bursts WHERE dataset = 'bgl' AND start_ts >= '2005-08-01 00:00:00' AND start_ts < '2005-09-01 00:00:00' GROUP BY 1 ), b_prev AS ( SELECT pattern_id, count(*) AS bursts_prev FROM bursts WHERE dataset = 'bgl' AND start_ts >= '2005-07-01 00:00:00' AND start_ts < '2005-08-01 00:00:00' GROUP BY 1 ), base AS ( SELECT p.pattern_id, p.template, p.component, coalesce(o.team, 'unowned') AS team, p.severity, now.lines, now.problem_lines, now.nodes, now.weeks_active, coalesce(b_now.bursts, 0) AS bursts, coalesce(b_prev.bursts_prev, 0) AS bursts_prev, coalesce(b_now.bursts, 0) - coalesce(b_prev.bursts_prev, 0) AS change, round(top_node.top_node_lines::DOUBLE / now.lines, 3) AS top_node_share, p.first_ts AS first_seen, p.first_ts >= '2005-08-01 00:00:00' AS new, round(j.p_fault, 3) AS p_fault, round(j.p_dump, 3) AS p_dump, round(j.p_problem, 3) AS p_problem, round(j.p_threat, 3) AS p_threat, j.kind FROM now JOIN patterns p ON p.dataset = 'bgl' AND p.pattern_id = now.pattern_id LEFT JOIN pattern_judgments j ON j.dataset = 'bgl' AND j.pattern_id = now.pattern_id LEFT JOIN ownership o ON o.dataset = 'bgl' AND o.component = p.component LEFT JOIN top_node ON top_node.pattern_id = now.pattern_id LEFT JOIN b_now ON b_now.pattern_id = now.pattern_id LEFT JOIN b_prev ON b_prev.pattern_id = now.pattern_id WHERE TRUE AND now.problem_lines > 0 AND j.p_problem >= 0.5 ), inputs AS ( SELECT *, round(weeks_active::DOUBLE / 5, 3) AS persistence, round(problem_lines::DOUBLE / lines, 3) AS problem_share, p_problem AS severity_input FROM base ), ranked AS ( SELECT *, cume_dist() OVER (ORDER BY bursts) AS pr_frequency, cume_dist() OVER (ORDER BY change) AS pr_trend, cume_dist() OVER (ORDER BY nodes) AS pr_spread, cume_dist() OVER (ORDER BY persistence) AS pr_persistence, cume_dist() OVER (ORDER BY severity_input) AS pr_severity FROM inputs ) SELECT *, round(100 * (0.3 * pr_frequency + 0.2 * pr_trend + 0.25 * pr_spread + 0.15 * pr_persistence + 0.1 * pr_severity), 1) AS score FROM ranked ORDER BY score DESC, bursts DESC, pattern_id

new.text:
In 2018-01-01 to 2018-01-08 the failed root logins on LabSZ matched 102039 log lines from 214 distinct IPs. The top sources by log lines are ip:59.63.188.30 (28766), ip:183.63.110.206 (17340) and ip:58.242.83.25 (14383). These are log lines, not exact attempts, because 35393 of them are 'message repeated' summaries.
Scope: Dataset ssh (OpenSSH auth log, host LabSZ), 2018-01-01 00:00:00 → 2018-01-08 00:00:00, full-text filter 'Failed password root'. The top-IP list is truncated to 20 of 214 IPs. The sample search rows are truncated. The pattern split covers all matches and is not truncated. Log data ends 2018-01-07 17:22:01, and the year is assumed (Jan = 2018).
The query 'Failed password root' matched 102039 log lines on 1 node (LabSZ), first at 2018-01-01 00:12:30 and last at 2018-01-07 17:07:13.
The matches split into two message patterns: pattern 400011 (direct 'Failed password for root' lines) with 66646 log lines, and pattern 400015 ('message repeated' summaries) with 35393 log lines.
214 distinct IPs appear in the matching lines. The top 20 are listed, each seen on 1 node.
Top IPs by log lines: ip:59.63.188.30 = 28766 (2018-01-03 10:07:06 → 2018-01-05 12:22:59); ip:183.63.110.206 = 17340 (2018-01-02 19:15:56 → 2018-01-03 10:08:41); ip:58.242.83.25 = 14383 (2018-01-01 08:48:42 → 2018-01-02 17:13:42); ip:183.192.189.131 = 8670 (2018-01-03 00:57:51 → 2018-01-03 12:36:43); ip:218.65.30.30 = 8374 (2018-01-01 14:23:31 → 2018-01-02 11:12:24); ip:218.87.109.156 = 7135 (2018-01-03 15:01:58 → 2018-01-04 12:17:10); ip:182.100.67.120 = 6179 (2018-01-01 20:32:23 → 2018-01-02 11:31:34); ip:182.100.67.52 = 3389 (2018-01-04 03:43:34 → 2018-01-05 07:32:31).
The next IPs are much smaller: ip:183.192.189.133 = 614 log lines, ip:139.219.239.13 = 566, ip:123.235.32.19 = 499, ip:119.7.221.129 = 462, ip:60.2.12.12 = 435, ip:115.238.230.180 = 432.
The top IPs are active in mostly separate time windows. For example ip:58.242.83.25 ended 2018-01-02 17:13:42, while ip:59.63.188.30 started 2018-01-03 10:07:06.
Timeline of the first matching burst (sshd-3117, 74.82.254.191). Before, 00:12:28: 'reverse mapping checking getaddrinfo for 74.82.254.191.ifibertv.com [74.82.254.191] failed - POSSIBLE BREAK-IN ATTEMPT!' and 'pam_unix(sshd:auth): authentication failure; logname= uid=0 euid=0 tty=ssh ruser= rhost=74.82.254.191  user=root'. At, 00:12:30: 'Failed password for root from 74.82.254.191 port 44521 ssh2'. After, 00:12:43: 'message repeated 5 times: [ Failed password for root from 74.82.254.191 port 44521 ssh2]', then 'Disconnecting: Too many authentication failures for root [preauth]' and 'PAM service(sshd) ignoring max retries; 6 > 3'.
At 2018-01-01 00:16:06 a second source, 188.166.228.127, logged 'Failed password for root from 188.166.228.127 port 54998 ssh2'. Just before it, the same IP tried invalid users 'ubnt' and 'admin'.
Hypothesis: The failures may come from automated brute-force campaigns that rotate source IPs: one IP is active for hours to a couple of days, then the next one takes over. Several sources sit in neighbouring address ranges (the ip:182.100.67.x, ip:183.192.189.x and ip:218.65.30.x families). Would confirm: Check per-IP timelines for overlap and per-connection attempt cadence. Check whether the same usernames and passwords are tried across IPs. Confirm the range ownership with whois.
Unknown: The exact number of attempts per IP is not established. 'message repeated N times' lines each stand for several attempts but count as one log line, and the ledger only shows one example (5 times).
Unknown: It is not established whether the filter also matches 'Failed password for invalid user root' lines. Only 'Failed password for root' lines are shown in the samples.
Unknown: Whether any root login succeeded is not shown in these results.
Unknown: Only the top 20 of the 214 IPs are listed, so the remaining IPs are not broken down.
Unknown: Comparison with the usual rate or earlier weeks is not available in these results, so new versus recurring cannot be decided.
Unknown: Customer impact and cost are not in the logs.
Next step: Run a query on the ssh dataset for the same window that sums the repeat count from 'message repeated N times' for pattern 400015, grouped by IP, and adds it to the pattern 400011 line counts per IP. — The 35393 repeat-summary lines hide multiple attempts, so the line counts understate the true attempt counts.
Next step: Search the ssh dataset for 'Accepted password for root' or 'Accepted publickey for root' from the eight top IPs between 2018-01-01 and 2018-01-08. — The results show only failures. A success from these IPs would change the severity.
Next step: Run pattern_history on pattern 400011 for the full 28 days, and top_entities for the remaining IPs (beyond the top 20) with the same filter. — This gives the baseline needed to say whether the week is unusual, and covers the IPs outside the top 20 of 214.
