Across 2015-07-29 to 2015-08-26, 65 problem bursts were recorded: 35 owned by coordination-platform and 30 by client-connectivity. Investigate first the 'Cannot open channel to <N> at election address' pattern (coordination-platform). It was active in all 5 weeks and its log lines jumped to 1039 and 1378 on the last two days.
Scope: Dataset zookeeper, 2015-07-29 00:00 to 2015-08-26 00:00 (previous period 2015-07-01 to 2015-07-29). Problem patterns only (p_problem >= 0.5), bursts = recurrences with a 30-min gap. Results were not truncated (11 candidate patterns). The logs carry no node/host, so nodes = 0 means spread is unknown.
There were 65 problem bursts in the period: 35 for coordination-platform and 30 for client-connectivity.
All 30 client-connectivity bursts are in component NIOServerCnxn. Coordination-platform bursts by component: QuorumCnxManager 8, LearnerHandler 7, QuorumCnxManager$RecvWorker 7, Follower 6, Learner 5, QuorumCnxManager$SendWorker 2.
Pattern 'caught end of stream exception' (NIOServerCnxn, client-connectivity) had 18 bursts (previous period 0), 1670 log lines and 3 weeks active.
Pattern 'Cannot open channel to <N> at election address /<IP>' (QuorumCnxManager, coordination-platform) had 8 bursts (previous period 0), 2584 log lines and 5 weeks active.
Daily log lines for the 'Cannot open channel' pattern were 71 on 2015-07-30, 14 on 2015-08-07, 8 on 2015-08-10 and 10 on 2015-08-18. They then rose to 1039 on 2015-08-24 and 1378 on 2015-08-25.
QuorumCnxManager had bursts in every week: 4 in the week of 2015-07-27, then 1 in each of the weeks of 2015-08-03, 2015-08-10, 2015-08-17 and 2015-08-24.
NIOServerCnxn had 22 of its 30 bursts in the week of 2015-07-27, then 0, 2, 6 and 0 in the following weeks.
Pattern 'Unexpected Exception: ' (NIOServerCnxn, ERROR) had 9 bursts, 27 log lines and 2 weeks active (previous period 0 bursts).
Pattern 'Unexpected exception causing shutdown while sock still open' (LearnerHandler, ERROR, coordination-platform) had 7 bursts, 590 log lines and 2 weeks active (previous period 0 bursts).
All 11 problem patterns were first seen on or after 2015-07-29, and each has previous-period bursts of 0.
Of 48507 WARN log lines in the period, QuorumCnxManager$SendWorker accounts for 20780 and QuorumCnxManager$RecvWorker for 20778.
Pattern 'Connection broken for id <HEX>, my id = <N>, error = ' (RecvWorker) produced 10356 log lines in 1 burst and 1 week.
1. Quorum peers cannot open election channels ('Cannot open channel to <N> at election address'). It is the only listed pattern active in all 5 weeks, and its log lines jumped on the last two days of the period. — owner coordination-platform — 8 bursts (previous period 0), 2584 log lines, 5 weeks active; 1039 log lines on 2015-08-24 and 1378 on 2015-08-25. — Check whether the 2015-08-24/25 surge continues past the period end and which peer addresses are failing. Compare with the election and connection-broken patterns on the same days.
2. 'caught end of stream exception' on client connections. It is the most frequently recurring problem pattern. — owner client-connectivity — 18 bursts (previous period 0), 1670 log lines, 3 weeks active; NIOServerCnxn had 22 of 30 bursts in the week of 2015-07-27. — Find out which clients or sessions close their connections abruptly, and why recurrences continued in the weeks of 2015-08-10 (2 bursts) and 2015-08-17 (6 bursts).
3. 'Unexpected Exception: ' errors in NIOServerCnxn. — owner client-connectivity — 9 bursts (previous period 0), 27 log lines, 2 weeks active. — Pull the full stack traces and check whether they coincide with the end-of-stream bursts.
4. LearnerHandler 'Unexpected exception causing shutdown while sock still open'. It has the highest problem score of the top patterns (p_problem 0.903). — owner coordination-platform — 7 bursts (previous period 0), 590 log lines, 2 weeks active; 6 of the component's 7 bursts are in the week of 2015-07-27. — Check whether leader-follower sync dropped around the burst times and whether it correlates with the Follower and Learner exception patterns.
Hypothesis: The surge of 'Cannot open channel' lines on 2015-08-24 and 2015-08-25 may reflect an unreachable quorum peer or a network problem on the election port. Would confirm: Check peer availability, restart or network events and the election-port connectivity on those dates, and see whether the lines stop once the peer is back.
Hypothesis: The connection-broken, end-of-stream and leader-follower exception patterns in the week of 2015-07-27 may share one underlying network or leader-election disturbance. Would confirm: Align the timestamps of the first occurrences, which are mostly around 19:03 to 19:54 on 2015-07-29, and check for a leader change or restart at that time.
Unknown: Which ensemble member or host each log line came from, since nodes = 0 means spread is unknown.
Unknown: Whether previous-period bursts of 0 mean the problems are truly new or the logs do not cover that earlier period.
Unknown: Root cause, customer impact, downtime and cost are not in the logs.
Unknown: Whether the surge seen on 2015-08-24 and 2015-08-25 continued after the period ended.
Next step: Investigate the 'Cannot open channel to <N> at election address' pattern: list the failing peer ids and addresses, and check the peer's state on 2015-08-24 and 2015-08-25. — It was active in all 5 weeks and had 1039 and 1378 log lines on the last two days (ev-9438f4c0bb, ev-937f64ecb3).
Next step: Break down 'caught end of stream exception' by session and time. Review the 2015-08-10 and 2015-08-17 week bursts against the 2015-07-29 cluster. — It has the most bursts (18), and 6 of the NIOServerCnxn bursts fall in the week of 2015-08-17 (ev-937f64ecb3, ev-06ab3088f8).
Next step: Confirm log coverage before 2015-07-29, so the previous-period comparison of 0 bursts can be trusted. — All 11 problem patterns first appear in the period with previous-period bursts of 0 (ev-5ec499d666).

sql: WITH now AS ( SELECT pattern_id, count(*) AS lines, count(DISTINCT node) AS nodes, count(DISTINCT date_trunc('week', ts)) AS weeks_active, count(*) FILTER (WHERE (severity IN ('FATAL', 'FAILURE', 'SEVERE', 'ERROR', 'CRITICAL') OR severity IN ('WARN', 'WARNING') OR status >= 500 OR severity IS NULL)) AS problem_lines FROM logs WHERE dataset = 'zookeeper' AND ts >= '2015-07-29 00:00:00' AND ts < '2015-08-26 00:00:00' AND pattern_id IS NOT NULL GROUP BY 1 ), top_node AS ( SELECT pattern_id, max(n) AS top_node_lines FROM ( SELECT pattern_id, node, count(*) AS n FROM logs WHERE dataset = 'zookeeper' AND ts >= '2015-07-29 00:00:00' AND ts < '2015-08-26 00:00:00' AND node IS NOT NULL GROUP BY 1, 2) GROUP BY 1 ), b_now AS ( SELECT pattern_id, count(*) AS bursts FROM bursts WHERE dataset = 'zookeeper' AND start_ts >= '2015-07-29 00:00:00' AND start_ts < '2015-08-26 00:00:00' GROUP BY 1 ), b_prev AS ( SELECT pattern_id, count(*) AS bursts_prev FROM bursts WHERE dataset = 'zookeeper' AND start_ts >= '2015-07-01 00:00:00' AND start_ts < '2015-07-29 00:00:00' GROUP BY 1 ), base AS ( SELECT p.pattern_id, p.template, p.component, coalesce(o.team, 'unowned') AS team, p.severity, now.lines, now.problem_lines, now.nodes, now.weeks_active, coalesce(b_now.bursts, 0) AS bursts, coalesce(b_prev.bursts_prev, 0) AS bursts_prev, coalesce(b_now.bursts, 0) - coalesce(b_prev.bursts_prev, 0) AS change, round(top_node.top_node_lines::DOUBLE / now.lines, 3) AS top_node_share, p.first_ts AS first_seen, p.first_ts >= '2015-07-29 00:00:00' AS new, round(j.p_fault, 3) AS p_fault, round(j.p_dump, 3) AS p_dump, round(j.p_problem, 3) AS p_problem, round(j.p_threat, 3) AS p_threat, j.kind FROM now JOIN patterns p ON p.dataset = 'zookeeper' AND p.pattern_id = now.pattern_id LEFT JOIN pattern_judgments j ON j.dataset = 'zookeeper' AND j.pattern_id = now.pattern_id LEFT JOIN ownership o ON o.dataset = 'zookeeper' AND o.component = p.component LEFT JOIN top_node ON top_node.pattern_id = now.pattern_id LEFT JOIN b_now ON b_now.pattern_id = now.pattern_id LEFT JOIN b_prev ON b_prev.pattern_id = now.pattern_id WHERE TRUE AND now.problem_lines > 0 AND j.p_problem >= 0.5 ) SELECT *, count(*) OVER () AS candidates FROM base ORDER BY bursts DESC, nodes DESC, pattern_id LIMIT 15

sql: WITH now AS ( SELECT pattern_id, count(*) AS lines, count(DISTINCT node) AS nodes, count(DISTINCT date_trunc('week', ts)) AS weeks_active, count(*) FILTER (WHERE (severity IN ('FATAL', 'FAILURE', 'SEVERE', 'ERROR', 'CRITICAL') OR severity IN ('WARN', 'WARNING') OR status >= 500 OR severity IS NULL)) AS problem_lines FROM logs WHERE dataset = 'zookeeper' AND ts >= '2015-07-29 00:00:00' AND ts < '2015-08-26 00:00:00' AND pattern_id IS NOT NULL GROUP BY 1 ), top_node AS ( SELECT pattern_id, max(n) AS top_node_lines FROM ( SELECT pattern_id, node, count(*) AS n FROM logs WHERE dataset = 'zookeeper' AND ts >= '2015-07-29 00:00:00' AND ts < '2015-08-26 00:00:00' AND node IS NOT NULL GROUP BY 1, 2) GROUP BY 1 ), b_now AS ( SELECT pattern_id, count(*) AS bursts FROM bursts WHERE dataset = 'zookeeper' AND start_ts >= '2015-07-29 00:00:00' AND start_ts < '2015-08-26 00:00:00' GROUP BY 1 ), b_prev AS ( SELECT pattern_id, count(*) AS bursts_prev FROM bursts WHERE dataset = 'zookeeper' AND start_ts >= '2015-07-01 00:00:00' AND start_ts < '2015-07-29 00:00:00' GROUP BY 1 ), base AS ( SELECT p.pattern_id, p.template, p.component, coalesce(o.team, 'unowned') AS team, p.severity, now.lines, now.problem_lines, now.nodes, now.weeks_active, coalesce(b_now.bursts, 0) AS bursts, coalesce(b_prev.bursts_prev, 0) AS bursts_prev, coalesce(b_now.bursts, 0) - coalesce(b_prev.bursts_prev, 0) AS change, round(top_node.top_node_lines::DOUBLE / now.lines, 3) AS top_node_share, p.first_ts AS first_seen, p.first_ts >= '2015-07-29 00:00:00' AS new, round(j.p_fault, 3) AS p_fault, round(j.p_dump, 3) AS p_dump, round(j.p_problem, 3) AS p_problem, round(j.p_threat, 3) AS p_threat, j.kind FROM now JOIN patterns p ON p.dataset = 'zookeeper' AND p.pattern_id = now.pattern_id LEFT JOIN pattern_judgments j ON j.dataset = 'zookeeper' AND j.pattern_id = now.pattern_id LEFT JOIN ownership o ON o.dataset = 'zookeeper' AND o.component = p.component LEFT JOIN top_node ON top_node.pattern_id = now.pattern_id LEFT JOIN b_now ON b_now.pattern_id = now.pattern_id LEFT JOIN b_prev ON b_prev.pattern_id = now.pattern_id WHERE TRUE AND now.problem_lines > 0 AND j.p_problem >= 0.5 ) SELECT *, count(*) OVER () AS candidates FROM base ORDER BY bursts DESC, nodes DESC, pattern_id LIMIT 20

coalesce(b_prev.bursts_prev, 0) AS change, round(top_node.top_node_lines::DOUBLE / now.lines, 3) AS top_node_share, p.first_ts AS first_seen, p.first_ts >= '2005-12-01 00:00:00' AS new, round(j.p_fault, 3) AS p_fault, round(j.p_dump, 3) AS p_dump, round(j.p_problem, 3) AS p_problem, round(j.p_threat, 3) AS p_threat, j.kind FROM now JOIN patterns p ON p.dataset = 'apache' AND p.pattern_id = now.pattern_id LEFT JOIN pattern_judgments j ON j.dataset = 'apache' AND j.pattern_id = now.pattern_id LEFT JOIN ownership o ON o.dataset = 'apache' AND o.component = p.component LEFT JOIN top_node ON top_node.pattern_id = now.pattern_id LEFT JOIN b_now ON b_now.pattern_id = now.pattern_id LEFT JOIN b_prev ON b_prev.pattern_id = now.pattern_id WHERE TRUE AND now.problem_lines > 0 AND j.p_problem >= 0.5 ), inputs AS ( SELECT *, round(weeks_active::DOUBLE / 14, 3) AS persistence, round(problem_lines::DOUBLE / lines, 3) AS problem_share, p_problem AS severity_input FROM base ), ranked AS ( SELECT *, cume_dist() OVER (ORDER BY bursts) AS pr_frequency, cume_dist() OVER (ORDER BY change) AS pr_trend, cume_dist() OVER (ORDER BY nodes) AS pr_spread, cume_dist() OVER (ORDER BY persistence) AS pr_persistence, cume_dist() OVER (ORDER BY severity_input) AS pr_severity FROM inputs ) SELECT *, round(100 * (0.3 * pr_frequency + 0.2 * pr_trend + 0.25 * pr_spread + 0.15 * pr_persistence + 0.1 * pr_severity), 1) AS score FROM ranked ORDER BY score DESC, bursts DESC, pattern_id

sql: SELECT s.b AS bucket_start, count(x.t) AS bursts FROM generate_series(date_trunc('week', TIMESTAMP '2005-12-01 00:00:00'), TIMESTAMP '2006-03-01 00:00:00', interval '7 days') s(b) LEFT JOIN (SELECT b.start_ts AS t FROM bursts b JOIN patterns p ON p.dataset = b.dataset AND p.pattern_id = b.pattern_id LEFT JOIN ownership o ON o.dataset = p.dataset AND o.component = p.component LEFT JOIN pattern_judgments j ON j.dataset = p.dataset AND j.pattern_id = p.pattern_id WHERE TRUE AND j.p_problem >= 0.5 AND p.problem_lines > 0 AND b.dataset = 'apache' AND b.start_ts >= '2005-12-01 00:00:00' AND b.start_ts < '2006-03-01 00:00:00') x ON date_trunc('week', x.t) = s.b GROUP BY 1 ORDER BY 1

SELECT round(regr_slope(bursts, i), 3) AS slope, round(avg(bursts) FILTER (WHERE i < 14 / 2.0), 2) AS first_half_mean, round(avg(bursts) FILTER (WHERE i >= 14 / 2.0), 2) AS second_half_mean, sum(bursts) AS total FROM (SELECT row_number() OVER (ORDER BY bucket_start) - 1 AS i, bursts FROM (SELECT s.b AS bucket_start, count(x.t) AS bursts FROM generate_series(date_trunc('week', TIMESTAMP '2005-12-01 00:00:00'), TIMESTAMP '2006-03-01 00:00:00', interval '7 days') s(b) LEFT JOIN (SELECT b.start_ts AS t FROM bursts b JOIN patterns p ON p.dataset = b.dataset AND p.pattern_id = b.pattern_id LEFT JOIN ownership o ON o.dataset = p.dataset AND o.component = p.component LEFT JOIN pattern_judgments j ON j.dataset = p.dataset AND j.pattern_id = p.pattern_id WHERE TRUE AND j.p_problem >= 0.5 AND p.problem_lines > 0 AND b.dataset = 'apache' AND b.start_ts >= '2005-12-01 00:00:00' AND b.start_ts < '2006-03-01 00:00:00') x ON date_trunc('week', x.t) = s.b GROUP BY 1 ORDER BY 1))

SELECT team, round(regr_slope(n, i), 3) AS slope, sum(n) AS bursts FROM (SELECT t.team, s.i, count(x.t) AS n FROM (SELECT row_number() OVER (ORDER BY b) - 1 AS i, b FROM generate_series(date_trunc('week', TIMESTAMP '2005-12-01 00:00:00'), TIMESTAMP '2006-03-01 00:00:00', interval '7 days') s(b)) s CROSS JOIN (SELECT DISTINCT coalesce(o.team, 'unowned') AS team FROM bursts b JOIN patterns p ON p.dataset = b.dataset AND p.pattern_id = b.pattern_id LEFT JOIN ownership o ON o.dataset = p.dataset AND o.component = p.component LEFT JOIN pattern_judgments j ON j.dataset = p.dataset AND j.pattern_id = p.pattern_id WHERE TRUE AND j.p_problem >= 0.5 AND p.problem_lines > 0 AND b.dataset = 'apache' AND b.start_ts >= '2005-12-01 00:00:00' AND b.start_ts < '2006-03-01 00:00:00') t LEFT JOIN (SELECT b.start_ts AS t, coalesce(o.team, 'unowned') AS team FROM bursts b JOIN patterns p ON p.dataset = b.dataset AND p.pattern_id = b.pattern_id LEFT JOIN ownership o ON o.dataset = p.dataset AND o.component = p.component LEFT JOIN pattern_judgments j ON j.dataset = p.dataset AND j.pattern_id = p.pattern_id WHERE TRUE AND j.p_problem >= 0.5 AND p.problem_lines > 0 AND b.dataset = 'apache' AND b.start_ts >= '2005-12-01 00:00:00' AND b.start_ts < '2006-03-01 00:00:00') x ON date_trunc('week', x.t) = s.b AND x.team = t.team GROUP BY 1, 2) GROUP BY 1 ORDER BY bursts DESC

On node combo that morning, the kernel OOM killer fired repeatedly from 00:00:16 until 12:02:46. A clean shutdown for reboot began at 12:20:08 and the host came back up at 12:22:57. The logs show no OOM lines after the reboot, but they do not show why memory ran out or whether the OOM kills caused the reboot.
Scope: Dataset linux, node combo (1 distinct node), 2005-12-06 00:00:00 → 12:30:00 (837 log lines). Extra windows were 11:00–13:30 and 11:30–12:20:21 for the reboot. Several searches returned samples only (truncated); counts come from totals and count_by/trend, not the sample rows.
All 837 log lines in the window come from a single node, combo. Kernel is the top component with 639 log lines, and there are 54 components in total.
397 log lines contain 'Out of Memory', all from the kernel component. The first is at 2005-12-06 00:00:16 and the last at 2005-12-06 12:02:46.
OOM log lines per hour ran from 15 (08:00 hour) to 52 (02:00 hour) through the morning, with 29 in the 00:00 hour and 39 in the 11:00 hour. They fell to 16 in the 12:00 hour, which is cut off by the reboot.
The OOM kills hit httpd and python in repeated bursts. Verbatim, first line: 'Out of Memory: Killed process 7395 (httpd).' at 00:00:16. Later lines at 00:27:00, 00:27:04 and 00:27:09 kill sendmail (7135, 7270) and mrtg (7472).
At 00:27:23 the kernel logged 'httpd: page allocation failure. order:0, mode:0x1d2' followed by a 'Call Trace:' through __alloc_pages and do_page_fault. Four such failure lines fall between 00:27:23 and 00:27:36. A fifth, with mode:0xd2, appears at 05:01:26. These are the only non-OOM failed/failure/error/refused lines before 12:20.
The hour starting 12:00 has 389 log lines, against 15 to 78 in each of the earlier hours.
Before the reboot: the last OOM line is 'Out of Memory: Killed process 9864 (diskcheck).' at 12:02:46. Node combo has no log lines between then and 12:20:01. At 12:20:01 gpm logged '*** info [mice.c(1766)]: ', then 'Master rebooting...' (gdm) at 12:20:03, 'shutting down for system reboot' at 12:20:08, and 'Switching to runlevel: 6' at 12:20:14.
During shutdown (12:20:20 to 12:21:21) these services logged 'shutdown failed': messagebus, xfs, jserver, sm-client, named, rpc.statd and portmap. Others logged 'shutdown succeeded'. 'klogd shutdown succeeded' came at 12:21:26.
After the reboot: '1.4.1: restart.' (syslogd) at 12:22:57, followed by the kernel line 'Linux version 2.6.5-1.358 ...' at 12:22:57 and 'Memory: 125312k/129720k available ...' at 12:22:58. 'Failure registering capabilities with the kernel' was logged at 12:22:58.
After boot the only matches for the kernel/restart search are ntpd time-sync lines at 12:24:28, 12:27:44 and 12:28:50. The last log line in the window is at 12:28:50, and no OOM lines appear after the reboot.
The linux dataset has no ERROR severity. A severity filter for 12:22:57 → 12:30:00 returned 0 matches.
Hypothesis: The host may have been under sustained memory exhaustion all morning, with httpd and python workers repeatedly spawned and killed on a small-RAM machine (about 129720k). The reboot may have been an operator response to this. Would confirm: Compare OOM rate on earlier days with pattern_history for pattern 700495. Check memory/swap metrics and httpd worker settings. Look for any ticket or operator action around 12:20.
Unknown: Root cause of the memory exhaustion is not in these logs.
Unknown: These logs do not show whether the reboot was triggered by the OOM kills or was a planned or manual action. 'Master rebooting...' from gdm only shows it was initiated from the display manager session.
Unknown: Whether this OOM pattern is new or recurring was not measured. Only 2005-12-06 morning was queried.
Unknown: Why the node logged nothing between 12:02:46 and 12:20:01, and why 'Failure registering capabilities with the kernel' appeared at boot, is not established.
Unknown: Customer impact, downtime and cost are not in the logs.
Next step: Run pattern_history and spread for pattern_id 700495 ('Out of Memory: Killed process') on dataset linux for the days before 2005-12-06 to judge new vs recurring and the usual hourly rate. — The 397 OOM log lines are all from one node, but there is no baseline in these results.
Next step: Run search_logs on node combo for 2005-12-06 12:02:46 → 12:20:01 and the days before, and check httpd, python, sendmail, mrtg and diskcheck for what was spawning processes. — These processes are the OOM victims, and the 12:02:46 → 12:20:01 gap is unexplained.
Next step: Run precursors/search for 'Failure registering capabilities with the kernel' and for 'shutdown failed' (messagebus, xfs, named, portmap) across other boots on combo. — These failed shutdown steps and the boot-time failure line appear around the reboot and may be routine on this host.

On node combo the morning was dominated by repeated kernel Out of Memory kills (397 log lines of 837), with a page-allocation-failure trace at 00:27:23. The last OOM kill was at 12:02:46. The logs then show a clean, operator-style shutdown at 12:20:08 ("shutting down for system reboot") and a boot at 12:22:57 with no OOM lines after it up to 12:30.
Scope: Dataset linux, node combo (the only node), 2005-12-06 00:00:00 to 12:30:00, plus context windows around 12:20:08 and 12:21:30 to 12:40:00. All search results are truncated samples; counts come from total_matches and the facet.
837 log lines on 1 node (combo) between 2005-12-06 00:00:16 and 12:28:50; 639 of them are from the kernel component.
Pattern 700495 (kernel "Out of Memory: Killed process ...") accounts for 397 log lines, first at 2005-12-06 00:00:16 and last at 2005-12-06 12:02:46, on 1 node.
The OOM kills come in bursts. Sampled burst start times are 00:00:16, 00:05:18, 00:10:24, 00:15:25 and 00:20:18. The first line is "Out of Memory: Killed process 7395 (httpd)." The victims include httpd, python, sendmail (7135, 7270) and mrtg (7472).
At 00:27:23, right after the kills of sendmail 7135, sendmail 7270 and mrtg 7472, the kernel logged "httpd: page allocation failure. order:0, mode:0x1d2" followed by "Call Trace:" (__alloc_pages, do_page_cache_readahead, filemap_nopage, do_page_fault). The page allocation failure appears twice by 00:27:23.
Just before the reboot, OOM kills continued until "Out of Memory: Killed process 9864 (diskcheck)." at 12:02:46, preceded by "Killed process 9853 (mrtg)." at 12:02:41 and "Killed process 9715 (sendmail)." at 12:02:40.
The window before the shutdown line (12:00:08 to 12:20:08) holds 19 log lines on combo, not truncated. After the last OOM line at 12:02:46, the next line is at 12:20:01 (gpm "*** info [mice.c(1766)]: "), so no log lines appear between 12:02:46 and 12:20:01.
The reboot sequence: 12:20:03 gdm "Master rebooting..."; 12:20:08 shutdown "shutting down for system reboot"; 12:20:14 init "Switching to runlevel: 6".
During shutdown, several services logged failure: "messagebus shutdown failed" (12:20:20), "xfs shutdown failed" and "jserver shutdown failed" (12:20:29), "sm-client shutdown failed" (12:20:50) and "named shutdown failed" (12:21:10). Others logged "shutdown succeeded" (atd, privoxy, cupsd, gpm, httpd, sendmail, spamd, smartd, snmpd, xinetd, crond, apmd, ntpd).
The machine came back at 12:22:57: syslogd "1.4.1: restart.", "klogd 1.4.1, log source = /proc/kmsg started.", and kernel "Linux version 2.6.5-1.358 ...". Boot lines include "Memory: 125312k/129720k available (1540k kernel code, 3860k reserved, 599k data, 144k init, 0k highmem)".
Between 12:22:54 and the last line at 12:28:50, the 12:21:30 to 12:40:00 window holds 308 log lines. The OOM pattern's last occurrence in the 00:00 to 12:30 range is 12:02:46, so there are no OOM lines after the reboot in this range.
Hypothesis: The node is memory-starved: it reports 129720k total RAM, and httpd, python, sendmail and mrtg workloads repeatedly exhaust it. Bursts every ~5 minutes could come from a scheduled job or load pattern, and the OOM killer kept killing processes until an operator rebooted at 12:20. This is a possibility, not shown by the logs. Would confirm: Check cron/mrtg schedules and memory or swap metrics for combo at 5-minute marks. Compare OOM burst counts against earlier days with pattern_history for 700495.
Unknown: Who or what initiated the reboot (the logs show a normal shutdown path, not a crash, but not the trigger).
Unknown: Why no lines were logged between 12:02:46 and 12:20:01.
Unknown: Whether the OOM pattern is new or recurring, and its usual rate: no baseline was queried.
Unknown: Whether the OOM bursts stopped after the reboot or are only quiet in the first minutes, since logs end at 12:28:50 in this range.
Unknown: Service impact, downtime or customer impact: not in the logs.
Unknown: Exact burst count and per-process kill totals: only a 50-row sample was returned.

The linux logs for combo show no kernel panic in 2005-11-15 to 2005-12-01, and no reboot lines either. The only restart-like lines are two syslogd restarts (2005-11-20 04:09:36 and 2005-11-27 04:06:31). The dominant kernel signal is repeated out-of-memory kills of httpd, which the logs do not tie to any panic or reboot.
Scope: Dataset linux, node combo, 2005-11-15 00:00:00 → 2005-12-01 00:00:00. Filters: free-text searches for panic, reboot/restart/syslogd/Linux version, and kernel/oops/crash/OOM terms; pattern 700499 search; facet; pattern_history for 700495 (whole dataset 2005-06-09 → 2006-02-28). The OOM keyword search and the pattern 700499 search were truncated to a sample; counts come from totals.
Searching for 'panic' in linux over 2005-11-15 to 2005-12-01 returned 0 matches.
Searching for reboot/restart/syslogd/Linux version found 2 log lines, both on node combo, component syslogd, body '1.4.1: restart.': at 2005-11-20 04:09:36 and at 2005-11-27 04:06:31.
Around the 2005-11-20 restart: 04:08:59 'cupsd shutdown succeeded', 04:09:08 'cupsd startup succeeded', 04:09:36 syslogd '1.4.1: restart.', then 04:09:37 logrotate 'ALERT exited abnormally with [1]'. Only 5 log lines fall in the ±600 s window.
On 2005-11-27 the same order appears: 04:06:17 'cupsd startup succeeded' then 04:06:31 syslogd '1.4.1: restart.'.
Of 8675 log lines in the window, 8051 are from the kernel component. Pattern 700495 accounts for 6709 of them and pattern 700499 for 998.
Pattern 700495 ('Out of Memory: Killed process <N> <*>', component kernel, team linux-ops) starts at 2005-11-15 04:30:29 with the line 'Out of Memory: Killed process 28473 (httpd).' The kernel keeps killing httpd processes (e.g. 'Killed process 28474 (httpd).' at 04:35:29) over the following minutes.
Pattern 700495 is new: 2005-11-14 and every earlier day shown have 0 bursts and 0 lines. Whole dataset: 133 bursts, 10404 lines, 1 node, last seen 2005-12-09 04:58:54, median gap between bursts 1:14:50.
Daily peak for pattern 700495 was 2005-11-20 with 9 bursts and 1637 lines, versus 3 bursts and 88 lines on 2005-11-15.

sql: WITH now AS ( SELECT pattern_id, count(*) AS lines, count(DISTINCT node) AS nodes, count(DISTINCT date_trunc('week', ts)) AS weeks_active, count(*) FILTER (WHERE (severity IN ('FATAL', 'FAILURE', 'SEVERE', 'ERROR', 'CRITICAL') OR severity IN ('WARN', 'WARNING') OR status >= 500 OR severity IS NULL)) AS problem_lines FROM logs WHERE dataset = 'healthapp' AND ts >= '2017-12-23 00:00:00' AND ts < '2018-01-04 00:00:00' AND pattern_id IS NOT NULL GROUP BY 1 ), top_node AS ( SELECT pattern_id, max(n) AS top_node_lines FROM ( SELECT pattern_id, node, count(*) AS n FROM logs WHERE dataset = 'healthapp' AND ts >= '2017-12-23 00:00:00' AND ts < '2018-01-04 00:00:00' AND node IS NOT NULL GROUP BY 1, 2) GROUP BY 1 ), b_now AS ( SELECT pattern_id, count(*) AS bursts FROM bursts WHERE dataset = 'healthapp' AND start_ts >= '2017-12-23 00:00:00' AND start_ts < '2018-01-04 00:00:00' GROUP BY 1 ), b_prev AS ( SELECT pattern_id, count(*) AS bursts_prev FROM bursts WHERE dataset = 'healthapp' AND start_ts >= '2017-12-11 00:00:00' AND start_ts < '2017-12-23 00:00:00' GROUP BY 1 ), base AS ( SELECT p.pattern_id, p.template, p.component, coalesce(o.team, 'unowned') AS team, p.severity, now.lines, now.problem_lines, now.nodes, now.weeks_active, coalesce(b_now.bursts, 0) AS bursts, coalesce(b_prev.bursts_prev, 0) AS bursts_prev, coalesce(b_now.bursts, 0) - coalesce(b_prev.bursts_prev, 0) AS change, round(top_node.top_node_lines::DOUBLE / now.lines, 3) AS top_node_share, p.first_ts AS first_seen, p.first_ts >= '2017-12-23 00:00:00' AS new, round(j.p_fault, 3) AS p_fault, round(j.p_dump, 3) AS p_dump, round(j.p_problem, 3) AS p_problem, round(j.p_threat, 3) AS p_threat, j.kind FROM now JOIN patterns p ON p.dataset = 'healthapp' AND p.pattern_id = now.pattern_id LEFT JOIN pattern_judgments j ON j.dataset = 'healthapp' AND j.pattern_id = now.pattern_id LEFT JOIN ownership o ON o.dataset = 'healthapp' AND o.component = p.component LEFT JOIN top_node ON top_node.pattern_id = now.pattern_id LEFT JOIN b_now ON b_now.pattern_id = now.pattern_id LEFT JOIN b_prev ON b_prev.pattern_id = now.pattern_id WHERE TRUE AND now.problem_lines > 0 AND j.p_problem >= 0.5 ), inputs AS ( SELECT *, round(weeks_active::DOUBLE / 3, 3) AS persistence, round(problem_lines::DOUBLE / lines, 3) AS problem_share, p_problem AS severity_input FROM base ), ranked AS ( SELECT *, cume_dist() OVER (ORDER BY bursts) AS pr_frequency, cume_dist() OVER (ORDER BY change) AS pr_trend, cume_dist() OVER (ORDER BY nodes) AS pr_spread, cume_dist() OVER (ORDER BY persistence) AS pr_persistence, cume_dist() OVER (ORDER BY severity_input) AS pr_severity FROM inputs ) SELECT *, round(100 * (0.3 * pr_frequency + 0.2 * pr_trend + 0.25 * pr_spread + 0.15 * pr_persistence + 0.1 * pr_severity), 1) AS score FROM ranked ORDER BY score DESC, bursts DESC, pattern_id

sql: WITH now AS ( SELECT pattern_id, count(*) AS lines, count(DISTINCT node) AS nodes, count(DISTINCT date_trunc('week', ts)) AS weeks_active, count(*) FILTER (WHERE (severity IN ('FATAL', 'FAILURE', 'SEVERE', 'ERROR', 'CRITICAL') OR severity IN ('WARN', 'WARNING') OR status >= 500 OR severity IS NULL)) AS problem_lines FROM logs WHERE dataset = 'healthapp' AND ts >= '2017-12-23 00:00:00' AND ts < '2018-01-04 00:00:00' AND pattern_id IS NOT NULL GROUP BY 1 ), top_node AS ( SELECT pattern_id, max(n) AS top_node_lines FROM ( SELECT pattern_id, node, count(*) AS n FROM logs WHERE dataset = 'healthapp' AND ts >= '2017-12-23 00:00:00' AND ts < '2018-01-04 00:00:00' AND node IS NOT NULL GROUP BY 1, 2) GROUP BY 1 ), b_now AS ( SELECT pattern_id, count(*) AS bursts FROM bursts WHERE dataset = 'healthapp' AND start_ts >= '2017-12-23 00:00:00' AND start_ts < '2018-01-04 00:00:00' GROUP BY 1 ), b_prev AS ( SELECT pattern_id, count(*) AS bursts_prev FROM bursts WHERE dataset = 'healthapp' AND start_ts >= '2017-12-11 00:00:00' AND start_ts < '2017-12-23 00:00:00' GROUP BY 1 ), base AS ( SELECT p.pattern_id, p.template, p.component, coalesce(o.team, 'unowned') AS team, p.severity, now.lines, now.problem_lines, now.nodes, now.weeks_active, coalesce(b_now.bursts, 0) AS bursts, coalesce(b_prev.bursts_prev, 0) AS bursts_prev, coalesce(b_now.bursts, 0) - coalesce(b_prev.bursts_prev, 0) AS change, round(top_node.top_node_lines::DOUBLE / now.lines, 3) AS top_node_share, p.first_ts AS first_seen, p.first_ts >= '2017-12-23 00:00:00' AS new, round(j.p_fault, 3) AS p_fault, round(j.p_dump, 3) AS p_dump, round(j.p_problem, 3) AS p_problem, round(j.p_threat, 3) AS p_threat, j.kind FROM now JOIN patterns p ON p.dataset = 'healthapp' AND p.pattern_id = now.pattern_id LEFT JOIN pattern_judgments j ON j.dataset = 'healthapp' AND j.pattern_id = now.pattern_id LEFT JOIN ownership o ON o.dataset = 'healthapp' AND o.component = p.component LEFT JOIN top_node ON top_node.pattern_id = now.pattern_id LEFT JOIN b_now ON b_now.pattern_id = now.pattern_id LEFT JOIN b_prev ON b_prev.pattern_id = now.pattern_id WHERE TRUE AND now.problem_lines > 0 AND j.p_problem >= 0.5 ), inputs AS ( SELECT *, round(weeks_active::DOUBLE / 3, 3) AS persistence, round(problem_lines::DOUBLE / lines, 3) AS problem_share, p_problem AS severity_input FROM base ), ranked AS ( SELECT *, cume_dist() OVER (ORDER BY bursts) AS pr_frequency, cume_dist() OVER (ORDER BY change) AS pr_trend, cume_dist() OVER (ORDER BY nodes) AS pr_spread, cume_dist() OVER (ORDER BY persistence) AS pr_persistence, cume_dist() OVER (ORDER BY severity_input) AS pr_severity FROM inputs ) SELECT *, round(100 * (0.3 * pr_frequency + 0.2 * pr_trend + 0.25 * pr_spread + 0.15 * pr_persistence + 0.1 * pr_severity), 1) AS score FROM ranked ORDER BY score DESC, bursts DESC, pattern_id

sql: SELECT s.b AS bucket_start, count(x.t) AS bursts FROM generate_series(date_trunc('day', TIMESTAMP '2017-12-23 00:00:00'), TIMESTAMP '2018-01-04 00:00:00', interval '1 day') s(b) LEFT JOIN (SELECT b.start_ts AS t FROM bursts b JOIN patterns p ON p.dataset = b.dataset AND p.pattern_id = b.pattern_id LEFT JOIN ownership o ON o.dataset = p.dataset AND o.component = p.component LEFT JOIN pattern_judgments j ON j.dataset = p.dataset AND j.pattern_id = p.pattern_id WHERE TRUE AND j.p_problem >= 0.5 AND p.problem_lines > 0 AND b.dataset = 'healthapp' AND b.start_ts >= '2017-12-23 00:00:00' AND b.start_ts < '2018-01-04 00:00:00') x ON date_trunc('day', x.t) = s.b GROUP BY 1 ORDER BY 1

SELECT round(regr_slope(bursts, i), 3) AS slope, round(avg(bursts) FILTER (WHERE i < 13 / 2.0), 2) AS first_half_mean, round(avg(bursts) FILTER (WHERE i >= 13 / 2.0), 2) AS second_half_mean, sum(bursts) AS total FROM (SELECT row_number() OVER (ORDER BY bucket_start) - 1 AS i, bursts FROM (SELECT s.b AS bucket_start, count(x.t) AS bursts FROM generate_series(date_trunc('day', TIMESTAMP '2017-12-23 00:00:00'), TIMESTAMP '2018-01-04 00:00:00', interval '1 day') s(b) LEFT JOIN (SELECT b.start_ts AS t FROM bursts b JOIN patterns p ON p.dataset = b.dataset AND p.pattern_id = b.pattern_id LEFT JOIN ownership o ON o.dataset = p.dataset AND o.component = p.component LEFT JOIN pattern_judgments j ON j.dataset = p.dataset AND j.pattern_id = p.pattern_id WHERE TRUE AND j.p_problem >= 0.5 AND p.problem_lines > 0 AND b.dataset = 'healthapp' AND b.start_ts >= '2017-12-23 00:00:00' AND b.start_ts < '2018-01-04 00:00:00') x ON date_trunc('day', x.t) = s.b GROUP BY 1 ORDER BY 1))

SELECT team, round(regr_slope(n, i), 3) AS slope, sum(n) AS bursts FROM (SELECT t.team, s.i, count(x.t) AS n FROM (SELECT row_number() OVER (ORDER BY b) - 1 AS i, b FROM generate_series(date_trunc('day', TIMESTAMP '2017-12-23 00:00:00'), TIMESTAMP '2018-01-04 00:00:00', interval '1 day') s(b)) s CROSS JOIN (SELECT DISTINCT coalesce(o.team, 'unowned') AS team FROM bursts b JOIN patterns p ON p.dataset = b.dataset AND p.pattern_id = b.pattern_id LEFT JOIN ownership o ON o.dataset = p.dataset AND o.component = p.component LEFT JOIN pattern_judgments j ON j.dataset = p.dataset AND j.pattern_id = p.pattern_id WHERE TRUE AND j.p_problem >= 0.5 AND p.problem_lines > 0 AND b.dataset = 'healthapp' AND b.start_ts >= '2017-12-23 00:00:00' AND b.start_ts < '2018-01-04 00:00:00') t LEFT JOIN (SELECT b.start_ts AS t, coalesce(o.team, 'unowned') AS team FROM bursts b JOIN patterns p ON p.dataset = b.dataset AND p.pattern_id = b.pattern_id LEFT JOIN ownership o ON o.dataset = p.dataset AND o.component = p.component LEFT JOIN pattern_judgments j ON j.dataset = p.dataset AND j.pattern_id = p.pattern_id WHERE TRUE AND j.p_problem >= 0.5 AND p.problem_lines > 0 AND b.dataset = 'healthapp' AND b.start_ts >= '2017-12-23 00:00:00' AND b.start_ts < '2018-01-04 00:00:00') x ON date_trunc('day', x.t) = s.b AND x.team = t.team GROUP BY 1, 2) GROUP BY 1 ORDER BY bursts DESC

Connection sshd-16980 looks like a real user's login, not an attack. The first password attempt failed, then zachary logged in from 218.17.80.182 and the session ran until 18:40:58. The logs cannot prove who was at the keyboard.
Scope: Dataset ssh, node LabSZ. Request sshd-16980 on 2017-12-15 00:00:00 → 2017-12-16 00:00:00. Wider checks: entity ip:218.17.80.182 over the whole corpus, and a 20-minute node context window (2017-12-15 10:28:55 → 2017-12-15 10:48:55). The request search and the IP search were not truncated. The 'zachary' text search was truncated to a sample of its matches.
Request sshd-16980 has 6 log lines on 1 node (LabSZ), first at 2017-12-15 10:38:55 and last at 2017-12-15 18:40:58.
Timeline, at: 10:38:55 'pam_unix(sshd:auth): authentication failure; logname= uid=0 euid=0 tty=ssh ruser= rhost=218.17.80.182  user=zachary'. 10:38:57 and 10:39:03 'Failed password for zachary from 218.17.80.182 port 60110 ssh2'.
Timeline, after: 10:39:04 'Accepted password for zachary from 218.17.80.182 port 60110 ssh2', then 10:39:04 'pam_unix(sshd:session): session opened for user zachary by (uid=0)'. At 18:40:58 'pam_unix(sshd:session): session closed for user zachary'.
Before this request, the preceding lines on the node belong to a different request, sshd-16977: 'Invalid user sugon from 52.80.34.196' at 2017-12-15 10:33:11, and 'Received disconnect from 52.80.34.196: 11: Bye Bye [preauth]' at 10:33:17. These come from a different IP and a different username.
After the session opened, the next lines on the node belong to a different request, sshd-17102: 'Invalid user butter from 185.165.29.140' at 2017-12-15 10:46:08, followed by a failed password and a preauth disconnect from that IP. These are a different IP and username, not part of sshd-16980.
IP 218.17.80.182 has 20 log lines in the corpus, from 2017-12-11 16:48:51 to 2017-12-21 14:07:31, all on 1 node. Several requests show the same shape (a pam authentication failure, a 'Failed password for zachary', then 'Accepted password for zachary'): sshd-29120 on 2017-12-12, sshd-5459 on 2017-12-13, sshd-9262 on 2017-12-14, sshd-10647 on 2017-12-19 and sshd-19308 on 2017-12-21. The first line, sshd-23494 on 2017-12-11, is an 'Accepted password' line.
The same user zachary has an opened and closed session in the sample on each of these days: 2017-12-11, 2017-12-12, 2017-12-13, 2017-12-14, 2017-12-15 and 2017-12-19. The rows are a sample of 34 matches (truncated).
In this request the failures target only the valid user zachary from one IP and one source port, 60110. The login succeeded at 10:39:04. The failures were not 'invalid user' lines.
Hypothesis: A legitimate user (zachary) mistyped the password once or twice, then logged in successfully. The same IP and the same failure-then-success pattern recur on several days, which fits a routine working login rather than a brute-force run. Would confirm: Ask zachary whether 218.17.80.182 is their usual address, and check whether the same IP ever tries other usernames. If it does not, the legitimate-user reading holds. If zachary does not recognise the IP, treat the account as compromised.
Hypothesis: An attacker holding valid credentials for zachary could produce the same pattern. The first password attempt may have been a stale or guessed password. Would confirm: Check what zachary did during the session, from shell or auth logs, and whether the IP geolocates to the user's usual location.
Unknown: Who was actually at 218.17.80.182. The logs show no identity or ownership of the IP.
Unknown: What zachary did during the session from 10:39:04 to 18:40:58. These logs show only open and close lines.
Unknown: Whether password-only SSH login is the expected policy for this account.
Unknown: Rate versus the usual rate was not measured here. No customer impact or cost is in the logs.
Next step: Run search_logs with entity ip:218.17.80.182, then check whether the IP ever shows 'Invalid user' or failures for any username other than zachary. — The 20 log lines in the corpus show only zachary, but a short query confirms no scanning from this IP.
Next step: Ask zachary to confirm the 2017-12-15 login from 218.17.80.182 and the repeated daily logins. — The logs show a consistent pattern but cannot identify the person.
Next step: Inspect LabSZ shell history and auth records for the session sshd-16980 between 10:39:04 and 18:40:58, and consider moving zachary to key-based login. — Failed password attempts before success on a password-auth account leave the question open if the user does not recognise the IP.

sql: SELECT count(*) AS total_lines, min(logs.ts) AS first_ts, max(logs.ts) AS last_ts FROM logs WHERE TRUE AND logs.dataset = 'ssh' AND logs.ts >= '2017-12-11 00:00:00' AND logs.ts < '2018-01-08 00:00:00' AND logs.body @@ websearch_to_tsquery('"POSSIBLE BREAK-IN ATTEMPT"')

SELECT s.b AS bucket_start, count(c.ts) AS lines FROM generate_series(date_trunc('week', TIMESTAMP '2017-12-11 03:50:52.000000'), TIMESTAMP '2018-01-07 15:26:49.000000', interval '7 days') s(b) LEFT JOIN (SELECT logs.ts FROM logs WHERE TRUE AND logs.dataset = 'ssh' AND logs.ts >= '2017-12-11 00:00:00' AND logs.ts < '2018-01-08 00:00:00' AND logs.body @@ websearch_to_tsquery('"POSSIBLE BREAK-IN ATTEMPT"')) c ON date_trunc('week', c.ts) = s.b GROUP BY 1 ORDER BY 1 LIMIT 501

WITH now AS ( SELECT pattern_id, count(*) AS lines, count(DISTINCT node) AS nodes, count(DISTINCT date_trunc('week', ts)) AS weeks_active, count(*) FILTER (WHERE (severity IN ('FATAL', 'FAILURE', 'SEVERE', 'ERROR', 'CRITICAL') OR severity IN ('WARN', 'WARNING') OR status >= 500 OR severity IS NULL)) AS problem_lines FROM logs WHERE dataset = 'ssh' AND ts >= '2017-12-11 00:00:00' AND ts < '2018-01-08 00:00:00' AND pattern_id IS NOT NULL GROUP BY 1 ), top_node AS ( SELECT pattern_id, max(n) AS top_node_lines FROM ( SELECT pattern_id, node, count(*) AS n FROM logs WHERE dataset = 'ssh' AND ts >= '2017-12-11 00:00:00' AND ts < '2018-01-08 00:00:00' AND node IS NOT NULL GROUP BY 1, 2) GROUP BY 1 ), b_now AS ( SELECT pattern_id, count(*) AS bursts FROM bursts WHERE dataset = 'ssh' AND start_ts >= '2017-12-11 00:00:00' AND start_ts < '2018-01-08 00:00:00' GROUP BY 1 ), b_prev AS ( SELECT pattern_id, count(*) AS bursts_prev FROM bursts WHERE dataset = 'ssh' AND start_ts >= '2017-11-13 00:00:00' AND start_ts < '2017-12-11 00:00:00' GROUP BY 1 ), base AS ( SELECT p.pattern_id, p.template, p.component, coalesce(o.team, 'unowned') AS team, p.severity, now.lines, now.problem_lines, now.nodes, now.weeks_active, coalesce(b_now.bursts, 0) AS bursts, coalesce(b_prev.bursts_prev, 0) AS bursts_prev, coalesce(b_now.bursts, 0) - coalesce(b_prev.bursts_prev, 0) AS change, round(top_node.top_node_lines::DOUBLE / now.lines, 3) AS top_node_share, p.first_ts AS first_seen, p.first_ts >= '2017-12-11 00:00:00' AS new, round(j.p_fault, 3) AS p_fault, round(j.p_dump, 3) AS p_dump, round(j.p_problem, 3) AS p_problem, round(j.p_threat, 3) AS p_threat, j.kind FROM now JOIN patterns p ON p.dataset = 'ssh' AND p.pattern_id = now.pattern_id LEFT JOIN pattern_judgments j ON j.dataset = 'ssh' AND j.pattern_id = now.pattern_id LEFT JOIN ownership o ON o.dataset = 'ssh' AND o.component = p.component LEFT JOIN top_node ON top_node.pattern_id = now.pattern_id LEFT JOIN b_now ON b_now.pattern_id = now.pattern_id LEFT JOIN b_prev ON b_prev.pattern_id = now.pattern_id WHERE TRUE AND now.problem_lines > 0 AND j.p_problem >= 0.5 ) SELECT *, count(*) OVER () AS candidates FROM base ORDER BY bursts DESC, nodes DESC, pattern_id LIMIT 15

new.text:
These logs show a heavy password-guessing wave against root and invalid users during 2018-01-01 to 2018-01-08, but they do not show a successful root login, so root compromise is not confirmed. First step: have security-ops verify the accepted logins and the host itself, and decide on lockdown of root password login.
Scope: ssh dataset (OpenSSH auth log, host LabSZ), 2018-01-01 to 2018-01-08, compared with 2017-12-25 to 2018-01-01. Log ends 2018-01-07 17:22:01, and the year is assumed (Jan = 2018). Priority table is truncated: top 10 of 39 candidate patterns shown. The team roll-up covers all 39.
Team roll-up: security-ops is the only team, with 39 problem patterns, 1207 bursts (478 in the previous week, change 729) and 281388 log lines.
Log lines matching 'failed password for root': 102039 in the window versus 13488 in the previous week; first seen 2018-01-01 00:12:30.
Log lines matching 'too many authentication failures': 35318 in the window versus 1329 previously. Lines matching 'POSSIBLE BREAK-IN ATTEMPT': 14881 versus 1813. All three watches fired.
Daily 'failed password for root' log lines peaked at 31289 on 2018-01-03 and fell to 915 on 2018-01-07.
Searches for a root login found 0 log lines each: 'Accepted password' root in the window, 'session opened' root in the window, and 'Accepted root' over the whole dataset.
94 'Accepted' log lines occurred in the window, all on node LabSZ. Daily 'Accepted' lines were 0 on 2018-01-01 and 14 on 2018-01-02.
6 problem-type patterns were first seen in the window, each with 2 bursts or fewer.
1. Repeated 'Invalid user <*> from <IP>' attempts: attackers probing for valid accounts. — owner security-ops — 108 bursts (37 in the previous week, change 71), 1 node, 1 week active, 4340 log lines, score 100.0 — Decide whether to fund and approve exposure reduction for SSH (source restriction, rate limiting) and who owns the review.
2. 'Failed password for invalid user' guessing, the same attacker wave. — owner security-ops — 108 bursts (37 in the previous week, change 71), 1 node, 1 week active, 6130 log lines, score 100.0 — Approve a decision on disabling password login for root and invalid users, pending security-ops confirmation.
3. 'input_userauth_request: invalid user' pre-authentication rejections, part of the same wave. — owner security-ops — 108 bursts (37 in the previous week, change 71), 1 node, 1 week active, 4340 log lines, score 95.6 — Treat together with ranks 1-2 as one incident review, with security-ops to report whether any attempt succeeded.
Hypothesis: Root access may have been gained through a path not visible in this auth log (for example a different account later escalated to root, a key-based login, or tampered logs). Would confirm: Host-level review: login history, authorized keys, new accounts, privilege escalation records and file integrity checks.
Hypothesis: The 94 accepted logins in the window may be legitimate users and unrelated to the attack. Would confirm: Compare source IPs and usernames of the accepted lines with known users and with attacker IPs.
Unknown: Whether root was actually obtained: these logs show no successful root login, and root cause is not established.
Unknown: Cost, downtime and customer impact are not in these logs.
Unknown: Whether the attacker IPs that failed are the same ones behind any accepted login.
Next step: Review the 94 accepted log lines in the window by user and source IP, and cross-check against attacker IPs from the failed-password bursts. — No root login appears in the logs, but accepted logins exist and have not been attributed.
Next step: If compromise is suspected, isolate the host and run a host-level forensic check (login history, keys, accounts, integrity) outside the auth log. — The auth log alone cannot confirm or rule out root access.
Next step: Decide on hardening: disable root password login, restrict SSH sources, add rate limiting. — Failed-root-password log lines rose to 102039 from 13488 the previous week, and the log shows 108 bursts of invalid-user probing.

sql: WITH now AS ( SELECT pattern_id, count(*) AS lines, count(DISTINCT node) AS nodes, count(DISTINCT date_trunc('week', ts)) AS weeks_active, count(*) FILTER (WHERE (severity IN ('FATAL', 'FAILURE', 'SEVERE', 'ERROR', 'CRITICAL') OR severity IN ('WARN', 'WARNING') OR status >= 500 OR severity IS NULL)) AS problem_lines FROM logs WHERE dataset = 'ssh' AND ts >= '2018-01-01 00:00:00' AND ts < '2018-01-08 00:00:00' AND pattern_id IS NOT NULL GROUP BY 1 ), top_node AS ( SELECT pattern_id, max(n) AS top_node_lines FROM ( SELECT pattern_id, node, count(*) AS n FROM logs WHERE dataset = 'ssh' AND ts >= '2018-01-01 00:00:00' AND ts < '2018-01-08 00:00:00' AND node IS NOT NULL GROUP BY 1, 2) GROUP BY 1 ), b_now AS ( SELECT pattern_id, count(*) AS bursts FROM bursts WHERE dataset = 'ssh' AND start_ts >= '2018-01-01 00:00:00' AND start_ts < '2018-01-08 00:00:00' GROUP BY 1 ), b_prev AS ( SELECT pattern_id, count(*) AS bursts_prev FROM bursts WHERE dataset = 'ssh' AND start_ts >= '2017-12-25 00:00:00' AND start_ts < '2018-01-01 00:00:00' GROUP BY 1 ), base AS ( SELECT p.pattern_id, p.template, p.component, coalesce(o.team, 'unowned') AS team, p.severity, now.lines, now.problem_lines, now.nodes, now.weeks_active, coalesce(b_now.bursts, 0) AS bursts, coalesce(b_prev.bursts_prev, 0) AS bursts_prev, coalesce(b_now.bursts, 0) - coalesce(b_prev.bursts_prev, 0) AS change, round(top_node.top_node_lines::DOUBLE / now.lines, 3) AS top_node_share, p.first_ts AS first_seen, p.first_ts >= '2018-01-01 00:00:00' AS new, round(j.p_fault, 3) AS p_fault, round(j.p_dump, 3) AS p_dump, round(j.p_problem, 3) AS p_problem, round(j.p_threat, 3) AS p_threat, j.kind FROM now JOIN patterns p ON p.dataset = 'ssh' AND p.pattern_id = now.pattern_id LEFT JOIN pattern_judgments j ON j.dataset = 'ssh' AND j.pattern_id = now.pattern_id LEFT JOIN ownership o ON o.dataset = 'ssh' AND o.component = p.component LEFT JOIN top_node ON top_node.pattern_id = now.pattern_id LEFT JOIN b_now ON b_now.pattern_id = now.pattern_id LEFT JOIN b_prev ON b_prev.pattern_id = now.pattern_id WHERE TRUE AND now.problem_lines > 0 AND j.p_problem >= 0.5 ), inputs AS ( SELECT *, round(weeks_active::DOUBLE / 1, 3) AS persistence, round(problem_lines::DOUBLE / lines, 3) AS problem_share, p_problem AS severity_input FROM base ), ranked AS ( SELECT *, cume_dist() OVER (ORDER BY bursts) AS pr_frequency, cume_dist() OVER (ORDER BY change) AS pr_trend, cume_dist() OVER (ORDER BY nodes) AS pr_spread, cume_dist() OVER (ORDER BY persistence) AS pr_persistence, cume_dist() OVER (ORDER BY severity_input) AS pr_severity FROM inputs ) SELECT *, round(100 * (0.3 * pr_frequency + 0.2 * pr_trend + 0.25 * pr_spread + 0.15 * pr_persistence + 0.1 * pr_severity), 1) AS score FROM ranked ORDER BY score DESC, bursts DESC, pattern_id

These logs show a large, rising wave of failed SSH logins on one node (LabSZ), many aimed at root, but they do not confirm that attackers got root: a search for "Accepted root" found 0 log lines. The first step is for security-ops to review the 94 successful-login ("Accepted") log lines before deciding how far to escalate.

security-ops owns all 39 problem patterns: 1207 bursts this week versus 478 the week before (change 729), across 281388 log lines.

The top-ranked patterns all sit on 1 node in 1 week, with 108 bursts against 37 the previous week (change 71).
1. Repeated attempts to log in with usernames that do not exist ("Invalid user <*> from <IP>") — owner security-ops — 108 bursts vs 37 the previous week (change 71); 1 node; 1 week; 4340 log lines — Decide whether to fund immediate blocking of the source IPs (firewall or fail2ban-style rate limiting) and confirm that remote root login is disabled.
2. Failed password attempts for invalid users ("Failed password for invalid user <*> from <IP> port <N> ssh2") — owner security-ops — 108 bursts vs 37 the previous week (change 71); 1 node; 1 week; 6130 log lines — Decide whether to require key-only authentication on this server and who owns that change.
3. Pre-authentication invalid-user requests ("input_userauth_request: invalid user <*> [preauth]") — owner security-ops — 108 bursts vs 37 the previous week (change 71); 1 node; 1 week; 4340 log lines — Ask security-ops to confirm the attempts are the same campaign as ranks 1 and 2 and report which source addresses they come from.
Hypothesis: The activity may be an automated brute-force campaign that failed, with the 94 "Accepted" log lines being legitimate logins. Would confirm: Check the user and source IP on each of the 94 "Accepted" log lines against known admins.
Hypothesis: A root login may have succeeded but be worded differently from the "Accepted root" search, so the search missed it. Would confirm: Review every "Accepted" and "session opened" log line, in order of time, for root or unfamiliar users and IPs, and check the host's own auth and shell history.
Unknown: Whether any attacker actually obtained root access: these logs do not show it either way.

Unknown: The remaining 29 problem patterns beyond the top 10 were not itemised.
Next step: Review the 94 "Accepted" log lines on LabSZ for root or unrecognised users and source IPs, and compare timing with the 2018-01-03 peak. — This is the only evidence that could show a successful login, since "Accepted root" returned 0 log lines.
Next step: Until the review is done, treat the server as possibly compromised: restrict SSH to known IPs, disable root password login and rotate root and admin credentials. — Failed-login bursts rose from 478 to 1207 in the week, so exposure is high while compromise is unconfirmed.
Next step: Collect host-side evidence (login history, new accounts or keys, changed files) outside these logs. — These logs cannot show what an attacker did after logging in.

Pattern 300021 ("File does not exist") had 599 log lines, first 2006-01-08 02:12:47 and last 2006-01-08 18:39:08. A text search for "File does not exist" in ERROR lines matched 605 log lines.
Pattern 300020 ("Directory index forbidden by rule: /var/www/html/") had 42 log lines, first 2006-01-08 00:13:38 and last 2006-01-08 23:26:23. The sampled lines come from many different client IPs, for example 60.222.194.88 and 68.145.116.232.
Client 83.16.14.142 produced 23 log lines between 2006-01-08 02:12:47 and 2006-01-08 02:12:49. The first reads: "[client 83.16.14.142] File does not exist: /var/www/html/sumthin".

At 04:05:58 followed "jk2_init() Can't find child 30829 in scoreboard", "mod_jk child init 1 -2" and "mod_jk child workerEnv in error state 5". At 08:46:27 "jk2_init() Can't find child 2182 in scoreboard" appeared again.
Timeline around the 02:12:47 burst: before it, "[client 198.70.193.2] Directory index forbidden by rule: /var/www/html/" at 01:26:30. Hypothesis: The 04:05:56 jk2/mod_jk errors may come from an Apache or mod_jk restart or reload with a broken workers2 configuration (channel.jni, vm, worker.jni could not be created). That would be a separate cause from the client probes. Would confirm: Check what happened on the server around 2006-01-08 04:05:56 (restart/config change) and review /etc/httpd/conf/workers2.properties. Look at the lines before 04:05:56 with precursors for pattern 300010.

Unknown: The sampled lines show "Directory index forbidden" clients as many distinct IPs, but their intent is not visible in these logs.

Yes. 2006-01-08 had 1039 apache log lines against 216 across the previous 7 days, a ratio of 33.7. Most were ERROR lines from httpd, mainly 'File does not exist' and 'script not found' for awstats paths, sent in short bursts by a few client IPs (193.19.219.217, 61.134.40.151, 218.106.165.188).
Scope: Dataset apache, 2006-01-08 00:00:00 → 2006-01-09 00:00:00, compared with the 7 earlier 24 h windows 2006-01-01 → 2006-01-08. No other filters. The facet, top-IP and search results are truncated samples or top-N lists; counts come from total_matches.
The window had 1039 log lines (43.292 per hour). The 7 earlier windows had 216 log lines in total (1.286 per hour). The ratio is 33.7, the busiest earlier window had 89 log lines, and 0 earlier windows reached 1039.
Severity on 2006-01-08: ERROR 965 log lines, NOTICE 74 log lines. Component httpd accounts for 929 log lines; mod_jk has 49 and jk2_init() has 33.
Top patterns by log lines: 300021 (599), 300033 (132), 300042 (107), 300020 (42). The facet reported 32 distinct patterns and was truncated.
Verbatim samples: pattern 300021 '[client 193.19.219.217] File does not exist: /var/www/html/awstats/awstats.pl'; pattern 300033 '[client 84.155.141.86] script not found or unable to stat: /var/www/cgi-bin/awstats.pl'; pattern 300020 '[client 60.222.194.88] Directory index forbidden by rule: /var/www/html/'.
The top client IPs by log lines were 193.19.219.217 (253 log lines, 2006-01-08 16:42:20 → 16:42:38), 61.134.40.151 (233 log lines, 16:35:32 → 16:36:18) and 218.106.165.188 (198 log lines, 18:24:47 → 18:25:09). 27 distinct IPs were extracted in total, and the top-15 list was truncated.
Timeline around the 61.134.40.151 burst: the context query found no earlier lines in the 10 minutes before 16:35:32 (before_total 0). It started with '[client 61.134.40.151] File does not exist: /var/www/html/awstats/awstats.pl', then alternated with 'script not found or unable to stat: /var/www/cgi-bin/awstats.pl' lines from 16:35:33. Later lines include '[client 61.134.40.151] File does not exist: /var/www/html/xmlsrv' and '/var/www/html/wordpress' at 16:36:04, then '/var/www/html/blog' at 16:36:18.
After the 61.134.40.151 burst: 16:36:19 NOTICE 'mod_jk2 Shutting down' (also at 16:36:06), 16:42:00 '[client 219.147.185.1] Directory index forbidden by rule: /var/www/html/', then at 16:42:20 the 193.19.219.217 burst began with repeated awstats.pl 'File does not exist' lines.

The node field is empty for these lines (distinct_nodes 0), so there is no per-node view. The activity is concentrated in the httpd component.
Hypothesis: The spike may come from automated scanners probing for an awstats.pl script, plus other common paths (xmlsrv, wordpress, blog). Each scanner IP sent a dense burst lasting under a minute, and every request failed because the paths do not exist on this server. Would confirm: Check the Apache access log for the same IPs and timestamps (HTTP status, user agent, request line), and check whether /var/www/cgi-bin/awstats.pl or /var/www/html/awstats exists. sql: SELECT s.b AS bucket_start, count(x.t) AS bursts FROM generate_series(date_trunc('week', TIMESTAMP '2005-11-01 00:00:00'), TIMESTAMP '2005-12-01 00:00:00', interval '7 days') s(b) LEFT JOIN (SELECT b.start_ts AS t FROM bursts b JOIN patterns p ON p.dataset = b.dataset AND p.pattern_id = b.pattern_id LEFT JOIN ownership o ON o.dataset = p.dataset AND o.component = p.component LEFT JOIN pattern_judgments j ON j.dataset = p.dataset AND j.pattern_id = p.pattern_id WHERE TRUE AND j.p_problem >= 0.5 AND p.problem_lines > 0 AND b.dataset = 'apache' AND b.start_ts >= '2005-11-01 00:00:00' AND b.start_ts < '2005-12-01 00:00:00') x ON date_trunc('week', x.t) = s.b GROUP BY 1 ORDER BY 1

SELECT round(regr_slope(bursts, i), 3) AS slope, round(avg(bursts) FILTER (WHERE i < 5 / 2.0), 2) AS first_half_mean, round(avg(bursts) FILTER (WHERE i >= 5 / 2.0), 2) AS second_half_mean, sum(bursts) AS total FROM (SELECT row_number() OVER (ORDER BY bucket_start) - 1 AS i, bursts FROM (SELECT s.b AS bucket_start, count(x.t) AS bursts FROM generate_series(date_trunc('week', TIMESTAMP '2005-11-01 00:00:00'), TIMESTAMP '2005-12-01 00:00:00', interval '7 days') s(b) LEFT JOIN (SELECT b.start_ts AS t FROM bursts b JOIN patterns p ON p.dataset = b.dataset AND p.pattern_id = b.pattern_id LEFT JOIN ownership o ON o.dataset = p.dataset AND o.component = p.component LEFT JOIN pattern_judgments j ON j.dataset = p.dataset AND j.pattern_id = p.pattern_id WHERE TRUE AND j.p_problem >= 0.5 AND p.problem_lines > 0 AND b.dataset = 'apache' AND b.start_ts >= '2005-11-01 00:00:00' AND b.start_ts < '2005-12-01 00:00:00') x ON date_trunc('week', x.t) = s.b GROUP BY 1 ORDER BY 1))

SELECT team, round(regr_slope(n, i), 3) AS slope, sum(n) AS bursts FROM (SELECT t.team, s.i, count(x.t) AS n FROM (SELECT row_number() OVER (ORDER BY b) - 1 AS i, b FROM generate_series(date_trunc('week', TIMESTAMP '2005-11-01 00:00:00'), TIMESTAMP '2005-12-01 00:00:00', interval '7 days') s(b)) s CROSS JOIN (SELECT DISTINCT coalesce(o.team, 'unowned') AS team FROM bursts b JOIN patterns p ON p.dataset = b.dataset AND p.pattern_id = b.pattern_id LEFT JOIN ownership o ON o.dataset = p.dataset AND o.component = p.component LEFT JOIN pattern_judgments j ON j.dataset = p.dataset AND j.pattern_id = p.pattern_id WHERE TRUE AND j.p_problem >= 0.5 AND p.problem_lines > 0 AND b.dataset = 'apache' AND b.start_ts >= '2005-11-01 00:00:00' AND b.start_ts < '2005-12-01 00:00:00') t LEFT JOIN (SELECT b.start_ts AS t, coalesce(o.team, 'unowned') AS team FROM bursts b JOIN patterns p ON p.dataset = b.dataset AND p.pattern_id = b.pattern_id LEFT JOIN ownership o ON o.dataset = p.dataset AND o.component = p.component LEFT JOIN pattern_judgments j ON j.dataset = p.dataset AND j.pattern_id = p.pattern_id WHERE TRUE AND j.p_problem >= 0.5 AND p.problem_lines > 0 AND b.dataset = 'apache' AND b.start_ts >= '2005-11-01 00:00:00' AND b.start_ts < '2005-12-01 00:00:00') x ON date_trunc('week', x.t) = s.b AND x.team = t.team GROUP BY 1, 2) GROUP BY 1 ORDER BY bursts DESC

Hypothesis: The 6 matching lines each in Learner and LearnerHandler may relate to snapshot sync between ensemble members, not local disk trouble. Would confirm: Read those lines in context and check whether they coincide with the coordination-platform problem bursts.

Payment failed first: at 2025-09-23 00:16:00.074 the payment pod logged ERROR "Visa cache full: cannot add new item." on node gke-clickstack-demo-demo-pool-50a4aa65-ilhf. The frontend then logged "Failed to place order" 0.003 s later, carrying gRPC code 13 with the same Visa cache message. Every earlier service in the trace (frontend, cart, currency, quote) logged only INFO.
Scope: Dataset otel; request_id 559cdb671a24df91566226b0d22afa4f, 2025-09-23 00:16:00.014 → 00:16:00.079 (one session, not truncated). Pattern history covers the whole dataset 2025-09-23 00:00:00 → 00:29:00.099. The rate check compares 00:11–00:21 against a single earlier 10-minute window (00:01–00:11, clipped because data starts at 00:00:00). The node context was truncated at 20 lines per side.
The trace has 13 log lines from 2025-09-23T00:16:00.014000 to 2025-09-23T00:16:00.079000 (duration_s 0.065), with 4 problem lines.
Before: frontend INFO "Checkout" at 00:16:00.014 on node gke-clickstack-demo-demo-pool-0280ddea-dsqn; cart INFORMATION "GetCartAsync called with userId={userId}" at 00:16:00.020755; currency INFO "Convert conversion successful" (5 log lines in total, the last at 00:16:00.054818); quote INFO "Calculated quote" at 00:16:00.051285.
Before the failure, payment (node gke-clickstack-demo-demo-pool-50a4aa65-ilhf) logged INFO "Charge request received." at 00:16:00.062000.
At: payment ERROR "Visa cache full: cannot add new item." (pattern_id 600010) at 00:16:00.074000, 0.012 s after "Charge request received." This is the first ERROR in the trace.
After: frontend ERROR "Failed to place order" at 00:16:00.077000; frontend ERROR at 00:16:00.078000: {"code":13,"details":"failed to charge card: could not charge the card: rpc error: code = Unknown desc = Visa cache full: cannot add new item.","metadata":{"content-type":["application/grpc"]}}; and the same text prefixed with ' ⨯ ' at 00:16:00.079000.
The trace touched 3 distinct nodes. The error originated on the payment pod payment-58fc8669d6-4d2tk; the frontend lines come from frontend-fc44b6cf9-zn2kp on a different node.
The same payment pod logged the same "Visa cache full" error for other requests in the same millisecond window, e.g. request 2c835b388ee31ec0507b93bddefb2a4a at 00:16:00.073000 and request 8ad5ee59a08bb31c75436c926439cbb9 at 00:16:00.074000. So this trace is not isolated.
Pattern 600010 (payment, payments-team, "job or application failure") has 11253 log lines in 1 burst across 24 nodes. It runs from 2025-09-23T00:00:00 to 2025-09-23T00:29:00.099000, and 5809 log lines precede 00:16:00. It is therefore recurring, not new at this time.
In the window 00:11–00:21, pattern 600010 had 3801 log lines (22806.0 per hour) vs 3617 in the earlier window (21702.0 per hour), ratio 1.1. The failure rate was roughly flat versus the immediately preceding window.
Hypothesis: The payment service's Visa card cache hit a capacity limit (or an injected or configured fault simulating it) and rejects every charge that needs a new cache entry, so checkouts fail at the charge step. Would confirm: Check payment service config, feature flags and source for the cache size and eviction. Check whether payment pods' memory or cache size plateaus from 00:00. Check whether non-Visa charges succeed.
Unknown: The logs do not show why the cache is full (leak, size limit, missing eviction, or an injected fault).
Unknown: The logs cannot establish customer impact, revenue loss or downtime.
Unknown: Whether the failure began before 2025-09-23 00:00:00 is unknown: the dataset starts there and the baseline is a single 10-minute window.
Unknown: These logs do not show whether non-Visa cards fail too.
Next step: Run a search on dataset otel, pattern_id 600010, grouped by node and minute from 00:00 to 00:29. Ongoing within the sampled 30 minutes, not a one-off blip: the "Visa cache full" card-charge error appears at a steady rate in all three 10-minute windows. The error comes from the payment component, which payments-team owns, but it surfaces mostly in frontend logs owned by web-frontend, which ranks first by priority score.
Scope: Dataset otel (sample: 0.1 s of every minute), 2025-09-23 00:00 to 00:30. "Visa cache full" matched 34187 log lines from 00:00 to 00:10, 34204 from 00:10 to 00:20 and 34224 from 00:20 to 00:30.
The payment component's pattern "Visa cache full: cannot add new item." (payments-team) has 11253 log lines across 24 nodes, in 1 burst, with change 1 versus the previous day (0 bursts).
The frontend (web-frontend) logs the same card-charge failure in several patterns, e.g. "failed to charge card ... Visa cache full" with 13051 log lines across 27 nodes in 1 burst.
Team roll-up (problem patterns / bursts / log lines): web-frontend 63 / 63 / 175115; payments-team 11 / 11 / 11540; checkout-team 5 / 5 / 2943; fulfilment-team 5 / 5 / 2375; catalog-team 6 / 6 / 110; shop-platform 3 / 3 / 5. All teams had 0 bursts the previous day.
1. Order placement fails in the frontend because the card charge fails ("Visa cache full: cannot add new item"). — owner web-frontend — 1 burst, 27 nodes, 13051 log lines, change 1, 1 week, score 98.4 — Decide with payments-team who leads the fix. The source of the error is the payment component, so web-frontend should confirm it only reports the failure.
2. The same card-charge failure appears again in the frontend's second error format. — owner web-frontend — 1 burst, 27 nodes, 13062 log lines, change 1, 1 week, score 97.8 — Treat it as the same issue as rank 1 and fund a single fix rather than two.
3. The email service raises "NoMethodError - undefined method each for nil". — owner fulfilment-team — 1 burst, 27 nodes, 2104 log lines, change 1, 1 week, score 97.2 — Ask fulfilment-team to assess it separately from the card-payment issue and decide its priority.
Hypothesis: A full cache in the payment service's Visa handling may be the cause of the failed charges, with the frontend errors as downstream symptoms. Would confirm: Check payment service cache size and eviction settings and metrics, and whether the errors stop after the cache is cleared or enlarged.

sql: WITH now AS ( SELECT pattern_id, count(*) AS lines, count(DISTINCT node) AS nodes, count(DISTINCT date_trunc('week', ts)) AS weeks_active, count(*) FILTER (WHERE (severity IN ('FATAL', 'FAILURE', 'SEVERE', 'ERROR', 'CRITICAL') OR severity IN ('WARN', 'WARNING') OR status >= 500 OR severity IS NULL)) AS problem_lines FROM logs WHERE dataset = 'otel' AND ts >= '2025-09-23 00:00:00' AND ts < '2025-09-24 00:00:00' AND pattern_id IS NOT NULL GROUP BY 1 ), top_node AS ( SELECT pattern_id, max(n) AS top_node_lines FROM ( SELECT pattern_id, node, count(*) AS n FROM logs WHERE dataset = 'otel' AND ts >= '2025-09-23 00:00:00' AND ts < '2025-09-24 00:00:00' AND node IS NOT NULL GROUP BY 1, 2) GROUP BY 1 ), b_now AS ( SELECT pattern_id, count(*) AS bursts FROM bursts WHERE dataset = 'otel' AND start_ts >= '2025-09-23 00:00:00' AND start_ts < '2025-09-24 00:00:00' GROUP BY 1 ), b_prev AS ( SELECT pattern_id, count(*) AS bursts_prev FROM bursts WHERE dataset = 'otel' AND start_ts >= '2025-09-22 00:00:00' AND start_ts < '2025-09-23 00:00:00' GROUP BY 1 ), base AS ( SELECT p.pattern_id, p.template, p.component, coalesce(o.team, 'unowned') AS team, p.severity, now.lines, now.problem_lines, now.nodes, now.weeks_active, coalesce(b_now.bursts, 0) AS bursts, coalesce(b_prev.bursts_prev, 0) AS bursts_prev, coalesce(b_now.bursts, 0) - coalesce(b_prev.bursts_prev, 0) AS change, round(top_node.top_node_lines::DOUBLE / now.lines, 3) AS top_node_share, p.first_ts AS first_seen, p.first_ts >= '2025-09-23 00:00:00' AS new, round(j.p_fault, 3) AS p_fault, round(j.p_dump, 3) AS p_dump, round(j.p_problem, 3) AS p_problem, round(j.p_threat, 3) AS p_threat, j.kind FROM now JOIN patterns p ON p.dataset = 'otel' AND p.pattern_id = now.pattern_id LEFT JOIN pattern_judgments j ON j.dataset = 'otel' AND j.pattern_id = now.pattern_id LEFT JOIN ownership o ON o.dataset = 'otel' AND o.component = p.component LEFT JOIN top_node ON top_node.pattern_id = now.pattern_id LEFT JOIN b_now ON b_now.pattern_id = now.pattern_id LEFT JOIN b_prev ON b_prev.pattern_id = now.pattern_id WHERE TRUE AND now.problem_lines > 0 AND j.p_problem >= 0.5 ) SELECT *, count(*) OVER () AS candidates FROM base ORDER BY bursts DESC, nodes DESC, pattern_id LIMIT 20

rows.title: Blue Gene/L supercomputer RAS logs (LLNL)
rows.description: Loghub BGL: reliability/availability/serviceability events of the Blue Gene/L supercomputer, 2005-06-03 to 2006-01-04 (214 days). Location = rack/midplane/node (R02-M1-N0-C:J12-U11: rack R02, midplane M1, node card N0, C = compute / I = I/O card). Components KERNEL, APP, MMCS, ... Alert labels exist for evaluation only.
rows.node_meaning: compute / I/O node: rack-midplane-nodecard-card-unit (C = compute card, I = I/O card)
rows.location_meaning: rack/midplane/node (first level = a whole rack, two levels = a midplane)

rows.title: OpenStack nova logs (cloud VM lifecycle and API)
rows.description: Loghub OpenStack: nova-api / nova-compute / nova-scheduler logs of a small cloud, 2017-05-16 to 2017-05-17, with request ids, tenant ids, VM instance ids, HTTP status and request latency inline. Some VMs had injected anomalies (labels for evaluation only).
rows.request_meaning: nova request id (req-…): one API call and the work it triggers
rows.object_meaning: VM instance uuid: follows one VM across requests and services (spawn, build, delete)
rows.status_meaning: HTTP status of nova-api requests (status: N in the message)
rows.duration_meaning: HTTP request time (time: N) and VM lifecycle step times (Took N seconds to spawn / build / delete)

rows.title: Zookeeper coordination service logs (one ensemble member)
rows.description: Loghub Zookeeper: Java log4j lines from a ZooKeeper ensemble member, 2015-07-29 to 2015-08-27. component = Java class, location = class/thread. Leader election, quorum connections, client sessions.
rows.location_meaning: Java class/thread, e.g. QuorumCnxManager/QuorumPeer[myid=1]_0.0.0.0_2181 (filter one class with its name alone)

rows.title: Apache httpd error log (one web server)
rows.description: Loghub Apache: error_log of one Apache httpd server, 2005-06-09 to 2006-02-28 (264 days). Levels notice / warn / error; client IPs inside messages are extracted as entities (ip:...). Multi-line messages inherit the previous line time and level.

rows.title: OpenSSH server auth log (host LabSZ)
rows.description: Loghub OpenSSH: sshd auth log of one internet-facing server (LabSZ), 28 days from Dec 10 (year not logged: Dec = 2017, Jan = 2018 assumed). No log levels (severity is NULL). Failed passwords, invalid users, break-in attempts; attacker IPs are entities (ip:...); request_id = sshd-<pid> = one connection.
rows.node_meaning: host name of the server (one host: LabSZ)
rows.request_meaning: sshd-<pid>: one SSH connection (process ids are reused over the 28 days, so one id can hold several sessions; request_timeline splits them)

rows.title: HDFS_v1 Hadoop file system logs (scale test, 11M lines)
rows.description: Loghub HDFS_v1: HDFS NameNode / DataNode logs of a Hadoop cluster over about 39 hours from 2008-11-09. request_id = the HDFS block id (blk_...), which follows one block across replicas; client and datanode IPs inside messages are entities (ip:...). Block-level anomaly labels exist for evaluation only.
rows.request_meaning: HDFS block id (blk_…): the whole life of one block across datanodes (allocate, receive, replicate, delete)

rows.title: OpenTelemetry demo app logs (slice of 1 B remote records)
rows.description: OpenTelemetry demo (microservices webshop on Kubernetes) logs from the public text_bench Parquet on S3 (part_000 = 1 billion records, first 30 minutes of 2025-09-23). This dataset holds 0.1 s of every minute of those 30 minutes; the full files are queried in place with the remote_* tools. component = service, location = namespace/node/pod, request_id = TraceId.
rows.node_meaning: Kubernetes node name
rows.request_meaning: OpenTelemetry TraceId (32 hex chars): one user request across services

rows.title: Linux syslog of one server (host combo)
rows.description: Loghub Linux: /var/log/messages of one Linux server (combo), Jun 9 to Feb 28 (year not logged: Jun-Dec = 2005, Jan-Feb = 2006 assumed). No log levels (severity is NULL). Kernel, sshd / ftpd / su authentication, udev, cron, named.
rows.node_meaning: host name (one host: combo)
rows.request_meaning: <program>-<pid>: one process (pids are reused over months; request_timeline splits sessions at quiet gaps)

rows.title: HealthApp Android app log (step counter and health data sync)
rows.description: Loghub HealthApp: log of an Android health app, 2017-12-23 to 2018-01-03 (dates not zero-padded in the raw file). No log levels (severity is NULL), no host. Components are app modules: Step_* = step counting, HiH_* = HiHealth data store and sync.
rows.request_meaning: app process id: all lines of one app process

sql: WITH b AS ( SELECT pattern_id, count(*) AS n, median(v) AS med, mad(v) AS mad, quantile_cont(v, 0.95) AS p95 FROM (SELECT pattern_id, duration_ms / 1000.0 AS v FROM logs WHERE dataset = 'openstack' AND pattern_id IN (SELECT DISTINCT pattern_id FROM logs WHERE dataset = 'openstack' AND duration_ms IS NOT NULL)) WHERE v IS NOT NULL GROUP BY 1 ), t AS (SELECT *, greatest(med + 6.0 * mad, med + 2.0) AS threshold FROM b ), f AS ( SELECT l.line_id, l.ts, l.pattern_id, l.object_id, l.request_id, l.duration_ms / 1000.0 AS value_s, l.body FROM logs l WHERE l.dataset = 'openstack' AND l.pattern_id IN (SELECT pattern_id FROM t) AND l.ts >= '2017-05-14 00:00:00' AND l.ts < '2017-05-18 00:00:00' ) SELECT f.line_id, f.ts, f.pattern_id, f.object_id, f.request_id, round(f.value_s, 3) AS value_s, round(t.med, 3) AS median_s, round(f.value_s / t.med, 2) AS ratio, f.body FROM f JOIN t USING (pattern_id) WHERE f.value_s > t.threshold ORDER BY ratio DESC, f.ts LIMIT 20

WITH b AS ( SELECT pattern_id, count(*) AS n, median(v) AS med, mad(v) AS mad, quantile_cont(v, 0.95) AS p95 FROM (SELECT pattern_id, duration_ms / 1000.0 AS v FROM logs WHERE dataset = 'openstack' AND pattern_id IN (SELECT DISTINCT pattern_id FROM logs WHERE dataset = 'openstack' AND duration_ms IS NOT NULL)) WHERE v IS NOT NULL GROUP BY 1 ), t AS (SELECT *, greatest(med + 6.0 * mad, med + 2.0) AS threshold FROM b ), f AS ( SELECT l.line_id, l.ts, l.pattern_id, l.object_id, l.request_id, l.duration_ms / 1000.0 AS value_s, l.body FROM logs l WHERE l.dataset = 'openstack' AND l.pattern_id IN (SELECT pattern_id FROM t) AND l.ts >= '2017-05-14 00:00:00' AND l.ts < '2017-05-18 00:00:00' ) SELECT t.pattern_id, p.template, t.n, round(t.med, 3) AS median_s, round(t.p95, 3) AS p95_s, round(t.mad, 3) AS mad_s, round(t.threshold, 3) AS threshold_s, count(*) FILTER (WHERE f.value_s > t.threshold) AS flagged FROM t JOIN patterns p ON p.dataset = 'openstack' AND p.pattern_id = t.pattern_id LEFT JOIN f ON f.pattern_id = t.pattern_id GROUP BY ALL ORDER BY flagged DESC, t.n DESC

WITH b AS ( SELECT pattern_id, count(*) AS n, median(v) AS med, mad(v) AS mad, quantile_cont(v, 0.95) AS p95 FROM (SELECT pattern_id, duration_ms / 1000.0 AS v FROM logs WHERE dataset = 'openstack' AND pattern_id IN (SELECT DISTINCT pattern_id FROM logs WHERE dataset = 'openstack' AND duration_ms IS NOT NULL)) WHERE v IS NOT NULL GROUP BY 1 ), t AS (SELECT *, greatest(med + 6.0 * mad, med + 2.0) AS threshold FROM b ), f AS ( SELECT l.line_id, l.ts, l.pattern_id, l.object_id, l.request_id, l.duration_ms / 1000.0 AS value_s, l.body FROM logs l WHERE l.dataset = 'openstack' AND l.pattern_id IN (SELECT pattern_id FROM t) AND l.ts >= '2017-05-14 00:00:00' AND l.ts < '2017-05-18 00:00:00' ) SELECT count(*) AS total_matches, count(DISTINCT f.object_id) AS flagged_objects FROM f JOIN t USING (pattern_id) WHERE f.value_s > t.threshold

WITH b AS ( SELECT pattern_id, count(*) AS n, median(v) AS med, mad(v) AS mad, quantile_cont(v, 0.95) AS p95 FROM (SELECT pattern_id, duration_ms / 1000.0 AS v FROM logs WHERE dataset = 'openstack' AND pattern_id IN (SELECT DISTINCT pattern_id FROM logs WHERE dataset = 'openstack' AND duration_ms IS NOT NULL)) WHERE v IS NOT NULL GROUP BY 1 ), t AS (SELECT *, greatest(med + 6.0 * mad, med + 2.0) AS threshold FROM b ), f AS ( SELECT l.line_id, l.ts, l.pattern_id, l.object_id, l.request_id, l.duration_ms / 1000.0 AS value_s, l.body FROM logs l WHERE l.dataset = 'openstack' AND l.pattern_id IN (SELECT pattern_id FROM t) AND l.ts >= '2017-05-14 00:00:00' AND l.ts < '2017-05-18 00:00:00' ) SELECT f.object_id, max(round(f.value_s / t.med, 2)) AS max_ratio, count(*) AS flagged_lines, min(f.ts) AS first_ts FROM f JOIN t USING (pattern_id) WHERE f.value_s > t.threshold AND f.object_id IS NOT NULL GROUP BY 1 ORDER BY 2 DESC LIMIT 50
