The panic was not on midplane R52-M0 in the logs: no R52-M0 location appears in the 13:00–15:00 window. The kernel panic ('rts panic! - stopping execution') is on node R52-M1-N9-C:J04-U11 in R52-M1, and it was the only node with a panic. Its dump starts with a machine check interrupt at 14:02:13.712395. The dump includes 'd-cache flush parity error........1', but the logs do not prove that was the root cause.
Scope: bgl, 2005-10-12 13:00:00 → 2005-10-12 15:00:00 (R52 hourly trend 2005-10-11 00:00:00 → 2005-10-14 00:00:00). Filters: location R52-M0, then node R52-M1-N9-C:J04-U11 and all locations. Results were not truncated except the get_context excerpts, which are limited to 10 lines each.
Searching 'kernel panic' with location R52-M0 in the window returned 0 matches, and counting log lines by severity for location R52-M0 returned total_lines 0.
Across all locations in the window there were 69 log lines in 7 locations. R52/R52-M1/R52-M1-N9-C:J04-U11 had 46 log lines; the other six locations were R67, R10, R30, R35, R40 and R06, with 10, 3, 3, 3, 3 and 1 log lines. None is R52-M0.
A synonym search for 'panic' in the window matched 2 log lines, both on 1 distinct node (R52-M1-N9-C:J04-U11), from 2005-10-12 14:02:18.479129 to 2005-10-12 14:03:26.118056. The last is 'rts panic! - stopping execution' (FATAL, KERNEL, pattern_id 69).
Node R52-M1-N9-C:J04-U11 had 46 log lines in the window, first 2005-10-12 14:02:13.712395 and last 2005-10-12 14:03:26.118056. All are FATAL from component KERNEL.
Timeline at the node. First line: 'machine check interrupt' (14:02:13.712395), then 'instruction address: 0x00016f20', then 'machine check status register: 0x81000000', then 'summary...........................1'. These are followed by the status dump, including 'd-cache flush parity error........1' (14:02:16.586071) while the other parity, plb and tlb lines read 0. After the dump come the register lines, 'special purpose registers:' and 'lr:0000f588 cr:84002444 xer:00000002 ctr:000003d5', and finally 'rts panic! - stopping execution' (14:03:26.118056).
Before the first line, the node had before_total 0 log lines in the preceding hour (from 13:02:13.712395), so there was no earlier warning on this node in that window. This is a new burst, not a continuation.
After the panic line, a context query across all nodes returned after_total 0 log lines within 600 s.
In the R52 hourly trend (2005-10-11 to 2005-10-14, 170 log lines in total), the 2005-10-12 13:00 bucket had 0 log lines and the 14:00 bucket had 46. Other R52 buckets with lines include 2005-10-12 09:00 (4), 2005-10-12 18:00 (32), 2005-10-13 05:00 (48) and 2005-10-13 23:00 (17).
A location search for R52-M1 returned total_matches 0 in the window, even though node R52-M1-N9-C:J04-U11 (location R52/R52-M1/...) has 46 log lines in that window.
Hypothesis: A cache parity fault (d-cache flush parity error = 1) on node R52-M1-N9-C:J04-U11 may have raised the machine check that ended in the RTS panic. Would confirm: Check whether earlier or later bursts of 'machine check interrupt' (pattern_id 33) or 'd-cache flush parity error' (pattern_id 42) occur on this node or its neighbours (pattern_history, precursors). Also check RAS/hardware records for this node's compute chip and whether it was replaced or reset.
Unknown: The logs do not show an R52-M0 panic; the user's midplane may be a mislabel of R52-M1, or R52-M0 events may be missing from this dataset.
Unknown: The location filter at the R52-M1 level returned 0 matches although the node's logs exist, so midplane-level location filters may not match as expected here and absence of R52-M0 lines is not fully conclusive.
Unknown: The root cause (hardware fault, job/application trigger, firmware) cannot be established from these log lines.
Unknown: Whether other nodes went down earlier is not shown: only this node produced panic lines in the window.
Unknown: Job, downtime and customer impact are not in these logs.
Next step: Run pattern_history and spread for pattern_id 33 (machine check interrupt) and 42 (d-cache flush parity error), and precursors for pattern_id 69, restricted to node R52-M1-N9-C:J04-U11 over a wider window than 2005-10-11 to 2005-10-14. — To see whether this is a recurring fault on the same node and whether it is local to one node, given a single node panicked in the window (ev-707426d7a4).
Next step: Re-run the location search with the full path 'R52/R52-M1/R52-M1-N9-C:J04-U11' and with R52-M0 sub-locations, e.g. count_by location with prefix R52 for 2005-10-12 13:00 to 15:00. — The R52-M0 and R52-M1 midplane filters returned 0 matches (ev-2c9ce2e62b, ev-920201a1df) while the node's logs exist, so the filter behaviour should be verified.
Next step: Inspect the R52-M1-N9 compute node and chip J04-U11 for hardware faults and check the job scheduler for what ran there at 2005-10-12 14:02. — The dump shows a machine check with a d-cache flush parity error at 14:02:16.586071 (ev-c1d60051d8).
